articles.title: Horn and Hardart
articles.content:
[h2]@[Bartholomew d'Larette](person:69f254be-aa76-4bbe-a9bb-37dae5034287), prop.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Bartholomew d'Larette](person:69f254be-aa76-4bbe-a9bb-37dae5034287) is a short, round little man, with thick grey hair and a moustache. He wears a tasteful, but not gaudy tunic, and hose and a cheerful smile. His family has managed the Horn and Hardart for four generations, and he is very much a traditionalist. Serving the inn's patrons is his life, and he allows nothing less than perfection in that service. Knows most of the elite by sight and name.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A handsome 3-story edifice of stone and half-timber on upper stories, with heavy oak shutters and colored glass in first floor windows. The inn is set within a small courtyard with a stone wall around the entire property and an iron gate. A large shield shaped sign is on the outside wall next to the gate, bearing the name of the establishment and a picture of a hardart wearing a crown.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The front door opens to a lobby with a high desk. Doors lead to the common-room, where meals and drinks are served, and ta comfortable sitting rooms. Stairs leads to upstairs rooms. Interior has smooth wood floors, with well-woven rugs in rooms. Walls are half-timber and plaster, with hanging tapestries. Magically glowing balls set in ornate iron wall sockets provide light in hallways, similar lights in rooms can be covered for darkness. Furnishings are not overly lavish, but are beautifully crafted and in excellent condition.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
Technically, the inn is open 24 hours a day. Major activity 4:00pm to 2:00am 6 nights a week (the nights Theaters are open)

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Expensive

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent, especially the food.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Contains [roll:2d10*10]gp. Kept in secret panel in d'Larette family quarters (ground floor, back wing of building).

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Dona @[Amelia d'Larette](person:12cd58b5-6587-4b0a-9120-6ea19a9e9e5e) is Bartholomew's wife. She is a plump and matronly woman, is a lover of music and theater, having grown up on @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870). She is involved more in running the inn than in direct contact with the guests. She spends a good deal of her time in the kitchen gossiping with @[Brisla Stoneaxe](person:fec6ca9c-c9e2-4773-906a-f3d24116222a) the cook. She knows everyone on @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870). She is the daughter of @[Artemis Guisto](person:804ce8e0-190f-4321-982f-5c304ed4b844), the Drum maker. She and Bartholomew have five children - Branden, Ophelia, Andrio, Carmen, and Petrio.  

@[Branden d'Larette](person:3e9caead-3ad4-4fb8-a26d-859dede12c08) is a chunky youth of 19, he is trying to learn the business of running the inn, but lacks his father's drive for perfection when he feels his service is not appreciated. He is in love with Felitia, a singer/actress who occasionally performs at the Horn and Hardart. He has an intense dislike of @[Paul de la Riis](person:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03), for the latter's flirting with Felitia, and will be less than gracious to any other offender.  

Brisla and @[Torvik Stoneaxe](person:f556a162-ff88-4c8f-9013-4d0b3ca283e7) - Brisla is the chief cook. A tall, hefty woman who speaks the Common tongue with an odd accent. She is bright and original with spices and herbs, adding to the Horn and Hardart's reputation for fine food. Torvik, her husband, tends the stable, grounds, and any other necessary manual work. Once a fine warrior until severely injured, he now walks with a pronounced limp, but has been known to disarm and bodily remove two of the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c) when they were causing too great a disturbance for even Bartholomew to bear.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
4 nights a week, there is a 75% chance that all rooms are taken. There is a 90% chance of the inn being full on weekends, without making reservations. 

One night a week, when Theaters are closed, the rooms will be only 10% taken, although the common room will be as busy as ever. 

Clientele are usually from well-to-do families of mercantile and nobility - although the two groups never mix.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Boccaccio de Kammeron](person:7987c903-5d74-4fd2-ba5a-b45ef9d76f18) | @[Rael Gavotte](person:1217ee33-13e6-4a14-8fdb-9755b8a993dc) | @[Portia Maggia](person:6b5a47fe-05ef-415d-82e8-3fc6f63fa142) | @[Anson Blackbourne](person:681f57c3-a3f7-4a8d-a44a-34b06fbbf06d) | The @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c) (not overly welcome)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Room price is 5gp per family member, and 2gp per retainer. Music and dinner are provided in the sitting rooms as requested, and in the common room.

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
Every evening there will be a performer in the common room, and these performers may be one of the following: Felitia (a lovely girl who performs a cappella from legendary epics, and plays lute). @[Robin O'Leary](person:a01786e8-604c-486c-8591-8716921489fe). @[Magda Cordovan](person:f21efac9-a5f1-4ea5-bb6d-1f4f21172263), @[Melisandre](person:3e36bdc2-4ec6-432d-b9bd-78ad5c800d64) [br][br] Note: Both this name and the  original name as published (Horned Hardart) are historical food and musical references. In the early 1900's,   [url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_%26_Hardart]Horn and Hardart[/url] was a chain of automat restaurants on the American east cost. [url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concerto_for_Horn_and_Hardart]Concerto for Horn and Hardart, S. 27[/url], is a composition by Peter Schickele aka PDQ Bach.

articles.title: House of Fagin Childstealer
articles.content:
[h2]Dealer in child labor[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Fagin, a wiry old half-elf with wild eyes, and a dozen others, have set up a thriving business in child labor, capturing "street rats" in the twisting alleyways and dark corners of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee). The ragged children, along with the occasional careless tiefling, are starved and beaten into submission, and sold for slave (indenture) labor in the workhouses of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) or @[The Commons](settlement:8ff1c19a-c29d-4050-9c7c-7200f23453be). Fagin and company live in the two-story wooden house, and their "merchandise" is kept in small cages in the cellar below until ready for sale. There are 3d6 children and 1d4-1 tieflings imprisoned there.

articles.content:
[h2]Spidersilk merchants[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Rohan Flanderin](person:c37f0b5b-8423-487a-9785-e63846ab8005)'s spidersilk empire is based in these four two-story houses of @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) with half-timbered upper stories that sits on Spidersilk St. running north from Dart St. A hanging sign outside one of the doors reads "House of Flanderin - Fine Silks and Fabrics" in Common. This door leads to stairs up to the offices and accounting-rooms of @[Rohan Flanderin](person:c37f0b5b-8423-487a-9785-e63846ab8005) and other administrative personnel where all the business of the spidersilk manufacturing and trading is carried on. Most of the space on the lower floors of the houses, which interconnect, is devoted to sorting and storage of spidersilk in the various phases of its manufacture. There is a wide alley behind the houses where deliveries and pickups are made by the many cottage workers the company employs and by the merchants and traders who deal in spidersilk. 

 The complex is constantly busy during the day, but unauthorized people will find it difficult (20% chance) to get into the heart of the warehouse area or the accounting offices without being challenged. At night the warehouses and offices are guarded by arcane sensing devices and alarms and 3 night watchmen who can signal the local Guard if anything appears amiss. 

 There is a safe in @[Rohan Flanderin](person:c37f0b5b-8423-487a-9785-e63846ab8005)'s office that contains 1d6x100gp for petty cash, and spidersilk itself is worth a great deal, although it is bulky and sticky in its raw form. 

 There is always a 20% chance that the company has openings for cottage workers with one of the following skills: Weaving, Spinning, and Dyeing. There is a 5% chance of an opening in the offices for an individual with skills in Bookkeeping. The company will only hire elves, however.

articles.title: House of Hofstra
articles.content:
[h2]Bankers and investment counselors[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The @[Hofstra Family](organization:4f2139cf-1498-4093-9f7b-4c3c3f7c8f75): @[Jaime Hofstra](person:3c39acd4-67f1-40a3-8ef1-ba378524e0f1) | @[Abel Hofstra](person:12a241b5-fcfe-4712-817f-0a12106d70e0) | @[Bakka Hofstra](person:b54d3eaa-536b-4110-a201-39e78fa5c9e9) | @[Charlie Hofstra](person:2a76cfbd-2b71-47b8-b505-c9cad32e55af) | @[Dauge Hofstra](person:985abb36-bd46-4191-a8d9-aaf0a14bade2)

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
Is a large two story @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) building that stands on a busy street corner. There are no windows on the first floor and those on the second story are all barred with iron grillwork. Over the door is a golden cutout sign of a coin, with the name "Hofstra" painted across it in black letters.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The first floor consists of a desk near the front door, guarded by a well-armed and healthy-appearing young man, with a locked, floor-to-ceiling set of bars behind him. Through the bars can be seen the enormous door of a large vault. A set of stairs ascends to the right. The second story is divided into a number of offices, with a pleasant appearing young woman stationed in the office at the top of the stairs, who will conduct a visitor to the proper office for the person with whom he wishes to deal.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
10:00am to 5:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Interest rates charged run from 2% to 8% per month, depending on the amount of the loan, and the reliability of the client.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
If investment is contemplated, the Hofstras have a number of different opportunities available, with interest paid from 4% to 40% per year. However, the higher the interest return, the greater the risk of loss - a 4% return would have only a 0.5% chance of loss, but the 40% return would have an 85% risk factor.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
The vault on the first floor.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Besides the Hofstras, there are half-a-dozen assorted bank  guards (Bank Guard 1, ) on duty at any given hour, and the receptionist on the second floor.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
One customer is seldom likely (5%) to see another.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Lots and lots of money, gold and silver coins, small gems, oodles of money.

articles.title: House of Rand
articles.content:
[h2]Banking, real estate, and commodities[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The Rand brothers.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A sturdy stone house of a single story has a sign over the front door. The sign is square, and shows a pile of golden coins, surmounted by the name "Rand".

[h2]Interior[/h2]
A tastefully decorated office occupies the entire first floor. There is a railing across the entire building about 4' from the door, behind which are six desks. The nearest desk is immediately behind the railing, and is occupied by a young man. The other five may, or may not, be occupied by the Rands and their clerks. At the back of the room can be seen a set of steps going down. These are guarded by two impeccably uniformed guards in armor with swords (scabbarded).

[h2]Hours[/h2]
11:00am to 4:00pm - the boys believe in short hours.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Much as the @[House of Hofstra](landmark:a159fe8a-2418-40b2-8003-ea222ae50808).

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Much as the @[House of Hofstra](landmark:a159fe8a-2418-40b2-8003-ea222ae50808). The only change normally encountered between one banking house and another are the results produced.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
The Rands' vault is down the stairs.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
The Rand brothers, the three clerks, and four @[Bank Guards](person:97351d5e-4403-45cd-8319-e0e2ed58abd5) at any given hour of the day. Six @[Bank Guards](person:97351d5e-4403-45cd-8319-e0e2ed58abd5) during non-business hours.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
There is a 35% chance of encountering other customers, one (75%) or two. These will usually be very wealthy people.

articles.title: Hrubilasz Riding Academy
articles.content:
[h2]Both steed and rider taught[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Bandolero Hrubilasz](person:c83f3003-0670-48fc-8f60-04143888a131) is an adequate trainer of horses and riders. What makes his academy worth its fees is his facility for selecting good men, then standing back and letting them work. Classes for horse and rider (in most cases, the two are trained together) are conducted on a daily basis over a period of six months. Some horses are trained to saddle by the men at the school, and these are usually sold at the auction when training is completed. 

Costs for courses at the school begin at 150gp a month, including boarding for the horse. The more complicated the course, the higher the price. Most men are satisfied with their steeds at the end of a course at Hrubilasz' school.

articles.title: Ironhoof Stables
articles.content:
[h2]Description[/h2]
Ironhoof Stables is a large fenced-in area a short distance outside the Copper Gate. Inside the pallisade there is an  office, and three barns housing the horses,  hay and feed. 

A large gateway sign is painted with horses on both sides and Ironhoof Stables in large lettering. The gate is kept closed with a simple latch and locked at night. 

Each barn  has six  stalls and storage areas for tools used to clean and maintain the stalls. Along the front and back walls, racks and shelves hold various equipment and supplies for both horse and rider. Bridles, saddles, stirrups, and reins hang neatly from hooks. 

A riding area in the front of the property is set up with various obstacles for training purposes. Horses stabled in the facility spend daily time in the riding area, being exercised and inspected for infirmities. Some undergo advanced training, learning to jump obstacles and handle quick movements, preparing them for warriors and hunters. Several water troughs are scatiered throughout the property.

The office is a larger structure with an inviting doorway. Inside, it has several tables,  some comfortable guest chairs, and several artworks depicting championship horses that have been stabled in the facility. 

[h2]People[/h2]
[h3]@[Cecil Ironhoof](person:1e5562af-61be-4c8a-a50b-e547650c3a2e)[/h3]
The owner, Sir Cecil, is an ex-cavalryman in his late fitiies with a rugged countenance marked by years of outdoor labor. He has piercing blue eyes that seem to miss nothing and a closely cropped beard streaked with gray. His hands are calloused from years of handling horses and working with tools, and his stance exudes an air of authority and confidence. He wears well-designed riding clothes and personally rides all the horses that enter his stables for training, evaluating them for suitability. 

He treats the stables and his workers as though they were his own litile unit, each in their regimented place, with a keen understanding of their tasks and expectations. He considers them all good people and trusts each implicitly to care for and protect these noble steeds, whatever the cost. He spends a few minutes chating quietly to each horse while feeding them apple slices. 

[h3]@[Vivienne Du Roche](person:6fc7368f-140b-48e8-9653-a9a5b530c503)[/h3]
Vivienne is an apprentice who comes from a noble family with horses in their blood. Her father served with Cecil in the cavalry, and they stable all their horses at Ironhoof Stables when they need some care or extra training before a show. Vivienne frequently worked with the family’s horses while boarded there, and eventually, Cecil asked if she wanted to join the crew. She accepted after consulting with and geting her father’s permission. 

Vivienne is still in her teens, with a slender, coltish frame and long chestnut brown hair worn in a single braid. She has keen brown eyes and an ever-present smile accentuating her freckled cheeks and perky nose. She dresses for the tasks at hand in simple work clothes or elegant riding outiits when she is scheduled to work with the horses in the exercise area. She is still integrating into the team and working hard to lose some of the harsh manners she learned while being raised as a proper noble of a reasonably high station. Despite these rough edges,  the down-to-earth workers all like her because of the care she shows their charges. 

[h2]Menu[/h2]
[row][col]
[b]Items[/b]
[ul]
[li]Bag of Oats: 2 sp
[li]Bale of Hay: 5 sp
[li]Bridle: 2 gp

[/ul][/col][col]

[li]Farrier Services (hoof trimming, per horse): 1 gp
[li]Grooming (per session, per horse): 1 sp

[li]Tack Repair: 1 gp
[li]Training Session (basic obedience, per horse): 5 gp
[/ul][/col][/row]
[h2]Rumors[/h2]
[ul]
[li]Cecil has a druid perform a secret rite before a mating visit and has had several prize-winning horses due to this touch of magic. 

[li]Horse thieves have been hiring local farms these past few months. Even Ironhoof Stables has hired night shift guards.

[li]Cecil maintains a secret training ground in the nearby woods where he personally trains batile horses for many of the knights of the realm. 

[li]Many believe Vivienne has the fabled skill of horse whispering because of her remarkable ability to train horses accurately and quickly. 

[li]The stables were a sacred burial ground centuries ago, and the horses still spook on foggy mornings.
[/ul]

[h2]Quest Seed: War Shoes[/h2]
Bards still sing of the mighty steed Midnight and his horseshoes that shot lighting bolts in batile when it reared up on its hind legs. The story credits Midnight with saving the king in a fierce batile that almost toppled the kingdom two hundred years ago. Midnight and its rider disappeared shortly atier that batile, never to be seen again. 

Today, a local net fisherman dredged up a horseshoe from the river, still as pristine as the day it was made. He thought it might be worth a few coins, so he brought it to the town farrier and was given five silver for it. The farrier examined it and couldn’t figure out what it was made of, certainly not iron. Not knowing what to do with it, he sold it to the town alchemist for ten gold pieces. The alchemist determined it was magical and had some lightning-based power, but it was incomplete. She brought it to her friend Cecil and wondered if it could possibly be one of the horseshoes the fabled horse Midnight wore in the batile that saved the kingdom. Cecil took it and promised to investigate. He is now seeking skilled treasure hunters who might be able to find the origin point of the horseshoe and perhaps recover the other three and maybe even Midnight’s bones to give it a fiting hero’s burial.

articles.title: Jasmine's House of Tattoos
articles.content:
[h2]Workshop of the Artist[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
A tiny hole-in-the-wall, with dirty windows. Yet @[Jasmine](person:6215423b-2e70-49f4-a8df-04d7c5ff4406) is a tattoo artist of renown, able to charge considerable amounts for her talents. She is a largish woman of indeterminate middle-age, with stringy brown hair, and is usually found in her shop, seated on a worn couch in front of a low table covered with needles, dye pots, etc. She pays local urchins to keep her apprised of the arrival of new ships in both the North and South docks. Her clientele consists primarily of officers, and the occasional seaman who has managed to save his meager earnings for a piece of her artistry. 

 @[Jasmine](person:6215423b-2e70-49f4-a8df-04d7c5ff4406) uses potent liquor as a painkiller when she works, and occasionally hears things not intended for her ears from her drugged clients. She rarely acts on this information, even though she is opposed to @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60) because of their excessive brutality, which she considers bad for business.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
Noon to Midnight

articles.title: Katzi's Dwarven Deli
articles.content:
[h2]Quick-n-Good[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
A stand up lunch counter serving quick filling fare (sausages wrapped in dark bread, beans and sauerkraut, boiled horsemeat with cabbage) and an endless stream of local gossip, both dispensed by the shop's rotund, constantly complaining, proprietor. In any given hour, @[Katzi](person:7a291be3-85ee-4809-ab99-e6f8d60cdf39) will kvetch about the weather, the price of meat, the tax rate, and the disrespectfulness of many of the clientele - in between, however, he is likely to pass along several morsels of useful information about local comings and goings, merchants holding sales, etc. @[Katzi](person:7a291be3-85ee-4809-ab99-e6f8d60cdf39)'s regular customers are 99+% dwarven, and the presence of non-dwarves around the counter will cause @[Katzi](person:7a291be3-85ee-4809-ab99-e6f8d60cdf39) to button up his otherwise flapping lip.

articles.title: Kelvar - Armorer
articles.content:
[h2]Excellent Armor[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Kelvar](person:bde8ced1-ce85-43cc-982d-d8b9d5597925) is the only dwarven artisan who chooses to work in @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b). He lives a solitary existence very near the city's North Gate, and it is said that his past holds some dark secret that makes him isolate himself from the rest of the dwarven community. Whatever his reasons are, his customers reward him handsomely for his services in his present locale, and his suits of chain and plate armor are usually worth their inflated price. There is a 70% chance that his goods will absorb 10% more hits than a normal suit of armor before it is rendered useless, and a 25% chance that they will absorb 25% more. @[Kelvar](person:bde8ced1-ce85-43cc-982d-d8b9d5597925) is very gruff with his customers and has no use for idle chatter. If a customer persists in asking @[Kelvar](person:bde8ced1-ce85-43cc-982d-d8b9d5597925) questions (especially personal ones), subtract 20% from the above stated chances of receiving an above standard product (and there is also a 10% chance that the armor produced by @[Kelvar](person:bde8ced1-ce85-43cc-982d-d8b9d5597925) under these conditions will absorb 10% less hits than a normal set).

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent

articles.title: Klekbek
articles.content:
[h2]'The Silver Mine' - Fine Metalworking[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Oin](person:8b4ebb01-167f-4f31-bfaa-733d491f0a51) is an irascible old dwarf with wispy grey eyebrows and beard, and stormy dark eyes. His fingers are gnarled with age, but his hands retain much of their metalworking skill. @[Oin](person:8b4ebb01-167f-4f31-bfaa-733d491f0a51) conducts business dealings solely in the dwarven tongue (a fact hinted at by the dwarven store name), and non-dwarves must get along as best they can. His tone is fearsomely stern, and may give the impression that he is greatly insulted when a customer attempts to bargain. In fact, he loves to haggle, and a buyer will get a much better price if he perseveres. His works are classical in styling, and finely detailed- in his shop, one will find bowls, trays, ceremonial masks, rings and belt buckles. All of beaten silver and gold. @[Oin](person:8b4ebb01-167f-4f31-bfaa-733d491f0a51) also has a shop along the Arcade, where some of his most unique works are on display.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent

articles.title: Konig - Master Armorer
articles.content:
[h2]Protection with Strength[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97) - is an embittered man, seeking to wreak vengeance on the cause of his unhappiness. He and @[Valli](person:34c3d4c1-63aa-40e4-84f3-ce75cdb96fee), the armorer located just up Ard Street and his former friend, wooed the same dwarven woman, who finally chose @[Valli](person:34c3d4c1-63aa-40e4-84f3-ce75cdb96fee). @[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97) is certain that @[Valli](person:34c3d4c1-63aa-40e4-84f3-ce75cdb96fee) used some trickery or enchantment to secure Soranal's love, and has sworn to drive his now enemy to bankruptcy, and has drastically lowered his prices and hired large numbers of additional help to do so. With so many new employees, @[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97)'s usual level of quality has fallen somewhat, but has not decreased so fast as his prices. @[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97) also has a shop in the Arcade and the proceeds from that enterprise help him to continue this brutal price-cutting war.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A large square building of stone. In the front, their feet set into stone bases, are three suits of finely honed armor of chain-mail, scale, and plate. The great helm accompanying the set of plate armor is decorated with a large pair of wings. A set of double doors lead inward, and are wide open during business hours. Currently, there are always 2-4 assistants walking the street in front of the shop, talking up the great sale prices available within, and emphasizing @[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97)'s reputation for craftsmanship.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
Within, all is a flurry of activity. In the main room, several more suits of armor are on display, and @[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97)'s assistants are busily fitting customers. In the back, a curtain divides the showroom from the work area, and the sounds of hammering, buffing, and welding echo through the shop from the rear.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
7:00am - 10:00pm

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Nominally Costly, at present Low/Fair

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Normally Excellent, at present Good/Excellent

[h2]Staff[/h2]
@[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97) and four assistants, journeymen armorers who are glad for the opportunity to work with him.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
The news of @[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97)'s campaign has begun to spread through the city, and the crowds at his shop are increasing by the day. The process of attracting a free sales clerk during the heaviest hours of traffic (from 11:00am - 1:00pm, or 4:00pm - 6:00pm) can become quite hectic, and one or two fistfights have occurred on the sales floor.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
@[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97) specializes in making armor of great strength. For a cost of 3x his normal rates, he can make a suit of chain armor that absorbs 4 hits of damage per successful blow (instead of the usual 2 hits), or plate armor that absorbs 6 hits per blow. These special items are not in @[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97)'s current price war.

articles.content:
[h2]A hill hiding a secret[/h2]

Aside from The Heights, this is the highest point in Haven. That's not saying a lot though as it's only about 75' above the Dorian. There's nothing special to see here above ground, it's what's below that is interesting. Kurgan's Hill is a part of Haven built on the remains of a much smaller city caslled Daria. Today, the few people that are aware of it call it the Forgotten City.

articles.title: Laudie Daly - Cooked Food
articles.content:
If you like barbecued meats on sticks, Laudie's is the wagon to patronize. Though her prices are a bit high (3-6sp a serving - depending on type of meat, pork up to chicken), the quality of the meat (she doesn't buy from Tekk) and the cooking (done on a charcoal brazier, and each stick lovingly basted) are unsurpassed. A serving includes a healthy slab of home-baked bread, and a dollop of any of six different sauces. 

Laudie is a gushing fount of information about happenings and people in the Market. She chatters constantly as she cooks, and will talk to anyone; questions asked of her generally receive more of an answer that the asker wished.

articles.title: Lorien Leathergoods
articles.content:
[h2]Nice leatherwork and tanning[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Sindra](person:9abadd16-8953-4112-b062-6922cdda7760) is a master leatherworker, a slender elven woman of youthful appearance (after all, she's only 240, hardly out of her teens). She is in union with @[Raf Poul](person:ebb79257-ab7d-4687-939a-9ae828fea67f), an associate of @[Nimrodel](person:c23b1ec6-6ac7-4c88-bff2-ef81a0a78957) the shipwright.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A pair of leather boots with an intricate sign reading "Lorien" hangs outside the front door. The building is a two level @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) structure, painted light green, with a large front window and several other smaller windows.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The first floor consists of a merchandise room, a leatherworking room, a dyeing room, and a large business office.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
9:00arn to 6:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
(1-2) Fair, (3-7) Good, (8-10) Excellent.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
A leather bag lies on a shelf in the rear working area. It contains [roll:1d10] x 1d10gp.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
@[Sindra](person:9abadd16-8953-4112-b062-6922cdda7760) makes most of the complicated clothing designs for customers who wish to purchase custom work. There are 4 youthful apprentices, one of whom is a level 2 thief trying to learn an honest trade, and a @[Callon](person:e39e1561-db4d-42df-a303-387740653cf7), a journeyman elf who does the less complicated leatherwork that @[Sindra](person:9abadd16-8953-4112-b062-6922cdda7760) has no time for. @[Raf Poul](person:ebb79257-ab7d-4687-939a-9ae828fea67f) occasionally helps @[Sindra](person:9abadd16-8953-4112-b062-6922cdda7760) with the bookwork, when he has free time.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
There are [roll:1d4] customers in the shop on the average (nearly half of them will be elves).

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Mirthule Conindir](person:57550327-6e3b-461f-8d5f-37f0d75ba55e) | @[Finsilivren Conindir](person:046e48b3-c811-4c77-b662-9701df18b3dd) | @[Regin A'Queen](person:90f261b7-8577-4c03-91e2-66f582e102ce)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
A lightly tanned but perfectly made leather jacket hangs in the front window. It bears the design of a strong dwarf with a pretty tavern girl slung over one shoulder (and a wineskin slung over the other). It is dwarf-sized and priced at 1,000gp.

articles.title: Lutes and Viols
articles.content:
[h2]@[Alfio Credenza](person:e95fe110-7ac2-4def-894a-539a3e0b78e9), prop.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The front room is small, and used for display of fine lutes, viols and psalteries. A bell on the door alerts Alfio when anyone enters. The shop employs eight journeymen and four apprentices. Only one of them, Nikklas, lives with Credenza's family upstairs.  

 Alfio has had a running feud with @[Luciano Clarino](person:2110a45a-d4b1-47c4-be2d-e35a52471a31) for 30 years, and will not abide even the mention of his name. He plans to marry his beautiful daughter Zofia to Nikklas in a few months, blissfully unaware that Zofia loves Derek Clarino, the son of his enemy, and Nikklas loves a different female every week. Nikklas, however, has no objection to the marriage because it will assure his position as heir.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Expensive

[h2]Quality[/h2]

articles.title: Maas Turkar - Weaponeer
articles.content:
[h2]Excellent Swords and Bows[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Maas makes swords, rapiers, and mace-type weapons himself. And acquires bows and pole weapons for sale in his shop from other craftsmen in the city. His own creations tend to be of good quality.  

 A customer can order a sword or mace crafted up to a maximum of +2 HP and/or +4 to damage (triple the base cost of the weapon ordered for each point of increase desired, waiting period 3 months).  

 There is also a 15% chance that a weapon of these types purchased from Maas' current stock will be +1 HP, but sold at normal cost. Bows and pole weapons purchased here are likely to be of fair quality with no chance of a random enhanced weapons.  

 Special orders of these items can be taken under the terms listed above (except that bows cannot receive damage bonuses), but the waiting period is 6-9 months, and there is a 25% chance that the finished weapon will not meet the desired specifications.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good/excellent.

articles.title: Mahti - Weaponeer
articles.content:
[h2]Weapons of Power[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Mahti](person:362e38fd-88b3-4afb-961b-d273f6600f29) - is a husky dwarf of middle age. He is so ugly that he keeps his face hidden from the world behind a bejeweled golden mask. He is quite an experienced adventurer, and still is interested in an occasional venture, if it is lucrative enough (i.e., if there is the promise of potent magical knowledge to be had at the end of the line). As a party member, and in daily social intercourse, @[Mahti](person:362e38fd-88b3-4afb-961b-d273f6600f29) is highly opinionated and frequently borders on the obnoxious. He is not overly fond of non-dwarves, and has an impressive array of insults for almost every race inhabiting Portal. However, he is fearless when the chips are down, and would carry with him a vast arsenal of mystical power.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A large rectangular @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) structure, about 40' long and 80' deep. Its walls are very thick. There are small round windows on either side of the heavy oaken door. Behind each is a small velvet-lined case, filled with a diorama of figures in full battle dress, squared off in fighting poses. Every 15 seconds or so the figures shift position, as their flashing weapons exhibit a variety of arcane powers. The whole effect is a very stunning (and sales inducing) visual display.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The shop is divided by paneling into over a dozen partially open cubicles. In each there are an array of weapons and arms and paraphernalia, all carefully labeled as to their powers (but without marked prices). A number of small metallic, sword-wielding spheres move irregularly through the cubicles. They keep an eye on the proceedings but also provide entertainment, for whenever they cross paths they launch into a mock combat. 

In the rear of the shop are two wooden doors. Both are normally barred. The left hand door leads to a weapon testing chamber, which is protected by a limited Null Magic Shield that greatly reduces the power of the enchantments encased in the weapons. The right hand door leads into @[Mahti](person:362e38fd-88b3-4afb-961b-d273f6600f29)'s enchanting chamber, which is filled with magical tomes and paraphernalia (and has a magical charge placed on the door which, if opened by any hand save @[Mahti](person:362e38fd-88b3-4afb-961b-d273f6600f29)'s, cuts loose with an arcane assault that feels like the electrified barbed wire fence, the killer guard dogs, and the pool of piranhas all rolled up into one).

[h2]Hours[/h2]
8:00am - 4:00pm (Evening visits may be arranged by appointment, at least 24 hours in advance.)

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly and Outrageous

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Who cares? Enchanters - especially high level enchanters - don't leave money in places where mortal men can get at it.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Only @[Mahti](person:362e38fd-88b3-4afb-961b-d273f6600f29)

[h2]Customers[/h2]
A steady stream of fighting men (between 8 and 20 at any one time). About 1/2 to 2/3 of these will be wistfully browsing rather than buying

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
Almost every high level fighter in the city has visited here at one time or another.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
GM's discretion - there is much potent magic here, with prices to match.

articles.title: Malbar Printing and Bindery
articles.content:
[h2]Books and printed matter[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Balin arn Malbar](person:c2f58cf3-93cc-4e8f-8516-a1976b867fb9) and his family have been in the bookmaking business (printing and binding, that is) since the dwarves of Gutenfast invented the movable- type printing press. Balin is a harried looking fellow, thinning hair perpetually mussed, and is constantly worried about meeting impossible deadlines. The print shop consists of several large buildings around a common courtyard with a stone wall and iron gates (locked after sunset), identified by a bronze plaque. Three large mastiffs patrol the courtyard and shop after hours, and two night watchmen are stationed just inside the front doors. There is little money kept on the premises, but the shop contains a small fortune in lead type, vellum, and other supplies. The only other items of interest are the 500 copies of the highly controversial paper, "Economic Progress into a New Age", by Professor Diego di Mantua, stored in the warehouse awaiting final delivery. Certain factions, such as the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c), would dearly love to destroy the books to keep them from circulation. 

 Balin, his brothers and their families have apartments nearby, and there is dormitory housing and a kitchen off the alley next to the complex for apprentices and journeymen. Besides Balin and his brothers, the print shop employs two dozen male dwarves, engaged in various steps of the printing and binding processes. The Malbar wives and daughters serve large meals for the whole staff at lunch (and dinner, for those who live in the dorm). Three of the apprentices and two journeymen are family members, as is one of the night watchmen. 

 @[Balin arn Malbar](person:c2f58cf3-93cc-4e8f-8516-a1976b867fb9)'s daughter Elorie is one of the girls sought by the Boltar brothers as wives. She spends a good deal of her day in the dormitory kitchen preparing meals for the print shop's employees.

articles.title: Malikor's Exchange
articles.content:
[h2]A trader in treasures[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Malikor](person:f4253e4a-7039-4b8e-a27c-037bb60b1e15) the Eye, so called for the patch he wears over his right eye, runs a pawnshop and fence out of the lower floor of this modest two-story wooden house. He specializes in precious metals, gems and jewelry, but will not look askance at almost anything of value, even if it is quite obviously "hot". @[Malikor](person:f4253e4a-7039-4b8e-a27c-037bb60b1e15) is a trained in Jeweler, Glassblower, and Silversmith, and knows a fake gem 80% of the time. He is (comparatively) honest with his clients, but if presented with items of extreme value by non-Guild members, has a 60% chance of trying to steal the items, possibly by force, or by substitution. He will usually offer 20% of the item's value, but can be bargained up to 40% for a "hot" item, and 60% for other items. @[Malikor](person:f4253e4a-7039-4b8e-a27c-037bb60b1e15) has around 2d4x1000 GP on hand at any one time, securely locked away in a hidden safe. 

 Should the players think to rob @[Malikor](person:f4253e4a-7039-4b8e-a27c-037bb60b1e15), they will find, to their regret, that the eye hidden under the patch is glass, imbedded with a PARALYZATION spell. All who meet its gaze must make a saving roll against INT, or be paralyzed for 1d12 hours.

articles.title: Martin Metals
articles.content:
[h2]Quality figurines[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Browin Treebeard](person:4c0d4fe9-907c-45f9-8239-087a69b08d0a) is the owner of this shop, which makes miniature pewter figurines, depicting dwarves in a variety of labors (including a number of fighting poses), and a number of real and legendary beasts. Though Browin has the physical appearance of a dwarf, he is actually an alien being from another sphere which has a portal that opens onto this world on rare occasions. The shop is the only two-story aboveground structure in @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954), and most of its neighbors view Browin and his employees as almost dangerously eccentric. Strange rumors abound that these figures sometimes move by themselves, acting in character with the form they depict (these rumors are, of course, unconfirmed, but anyone trying a figure of a dwarven thief or assassin is just asking for trouble, in my opinion). The shop advertises regularly in @[A. Gori Greataxe](person:e45f77bd-aace-4c5f-bf40-811011d61b14)'s newsletter, and there are also rumors that Browin is financing A. Gori's proposed expedition to find the bearded dwarven women (see Adventure Possibilities - The Dwarrow).

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High

articles.title: Melanie's
articles.content:
[h2]A hole-in-the-wall with delicious food[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Melanie](person:e2feb6d4-0cab-46cf-aeb3-7910e2ebf62d) is short, round, ruddy-faced, blonde-haired and hazel-eyed. She is an excellent cook, and serves meals three times a day. Her small kitchen has no menu - customers pay 2sp for whatever @[Melanie](person:e2feb6d4-0cab-46cf-aeb3-7910e2ebf62d) serves for breakfast or lunch, and 3sp for dinner. There is only seating for about 40 people at the long tables in the front room of her house, and the place is usually jammed (10% chance of finding a seat). Mealtimes are 6:30am to 8:30am for breakfast, 11:00am to 2:00pm for lunch, and 5:00pm to 8:00pm for supper. @[Melanie](person:e2feb6d4-0cab-46cf-aeb3-7910e2ebf62d) is assisted by her two daughters, Shalimar and Frangipani, both of whom are plump, blonde, and thoroughly married and proposition-proof. The girls do the majority of the customer service. 

 The customers are on the honor system, expected to drop the cost of the meal into a small box by the front door. If you can't afford to pay now, pay later (freeloaders are generally noticed after the first few times, and usually ejected by the regular clientele. For every attempt after the first, there is a cumulative 5% chance of it being noticed that one hasn't paid). Few customers freeload. They remember what it was like, trying to find good, cheap food before @[Melanie](person:e2feb6d4-0cab-46cf-aeb3-7910e2ebf62d) opened the place, and they don't want her to even think of closing.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Low, see above.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good to Excellent.

articles.content:
[h2]Boots, sandals, and shoes[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Meriwether is a decent bootmaker, and custom fits his work. An order requires 2d3 weeks to complete; 50% down is required with the order, and two additional fittings are required to ensure the comfort of the footgear. There are seldom more than two customers in the shop, and Meriwether, a small man, hunched from years of leaning over his work, usually has time to talk unless his mouth is full of tacks. He does know a good deal of gossip about the area, and the comings and goings of its residents, and can be an invaluable source of information (both the @[Thieves' Guild](organization:08dce3b2-80f7-468b-be7b-dd5fdbfac799) and @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60) use him for news of the North Corridor).

High.

[h2]Description[/h2]

She employs a regular network of 10-12 informants (mostly young dwarven men in their thirties and forties) who keep her informed of events in @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954). Frequently, however, a bride must be @[Imported](person:85c3b7a4-cbd6-48b9-9b32-6f7bdc14621b) from outside the city. An applicant's monthly percentage chance of finding a bride are equal to 1/3 x (CHA + APP, discounting racial adjustments) + 1% for each 1000gp he is willing to offer as a dowry.

articles.title: Minotaur Metalworks
articles.content:
[h2]Superbly crafted metal goods, with no bull[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Tacobur](person:c721435d-0ec1-4fd3-aeb0-6d498aafd814), the artisan, is unquestionably the best dwarven metalworker in Haven, and arguably the peer of Salvatore Cellini, the upstart Master of the Artisan's Guild. Unlike his discontented colleagues of that Guild, however, @[Tacobur](person:c721435d-0ec1-4fd3-aeb0-6d498aafd814) is unconcerned about the political struggle for Guild leadership, and largely minds his own affairs. He is an incredible perfectionist, who often consigns finished works that other artisans would give their eyeteeth to produce to the scrap pile (see below).

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A fairly large stone structure, with a sloped roof. Hanging above the doors is an immense bronze gryphon, incredibly realistic in every detail. There are two large ground floor windows, and a small opening in the attic. A silver bell hangs in the latter aperture. In each of the ground floor windows, a single large item is displayed (these items change every week, ranging from statuary to jewel encrusted bowls and chalices. All are breathtakingly beautiful).

[h2]Interior[/h2]
A set of velvet lined glass cases line the side and rear walls - each contains but one or two exquisitely crafted works of gold, silver, or platinum. A large revolving globe in the center of the room depicts the Three Continents of Gateway, with attached small miniatures representing major landmarks. A door in the rear of the room leads to the workroom, and is usually ajar.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
9:00am - 6:00pm

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly/Outrageous

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Superb +

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Wall safe concealed in the base of the wall - lock of Complexity Level 5.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
@[Tacobur](person:c721435d-0ec1-4fd3-aeb0-6d498aafd814) has one assistant metalworker, @[Vassig](person:4a6903a0-9414-4c5d-950b-e802a3ae3c83), who is constantly imploring @[Tacobur](person:c721435d-0ec1-4fd3-aeb0-6d498aafd814) (unsuccessfully) to become involved with the other @[Disaffected Artisans](organization:61f0b977-2ded-4c78-9624-06db0fe627f1). Whenever possible, @[Vassig](person:4a6903a0-9414-4c5d-950b-e802a3ae3c83) tries to rescue @[Tacobur](person:c721435d-0ec1-4fd3-aeb0-6d498aafd814)'s rejects from the trash pile before they can be thrown back in the smelter and re-melted. He smuggles these pieces out of @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954), and has them sold at Thieves Market (to conceal the origin of these goods, @[Vassig](person:4a6903a0-9414-4c5d-950b-e802a3ae3c83) etches the additional letters "rito" at the end of the artisan's original signature).

[h2]Customers[/h2]
[roll:1d100] 
- 01-35 indicates 1 customer in the shop; 
- 36-60, 2 customers; 
- 61-80, [roll:1d4+1] customers;
- 81-00, [roll:2d6] customers.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
There are many loiterers around the window displays, most of who realize that the works they covet are far beyond their modest means.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Bethli](person:5d5a4b6e-bd15-4afb-8d94-fdfe0f7d6b02) | @[Ralki](person:2c4d43b1-b3fd-415d-8b88-306af9a7386d)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Anything that gets past @[Tacobur](person:c721435d-0ec1-4fd3-aeb0-6d498aafd814)'s stringent scrutiny is a special piece of work.

articles.title: Mixolydian Mode
articles.content:
[h2]A Tavern[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Ranna Campanella](person:86dd6def-f658-404d-aafb-0192a9ce8ebd) is a fat, jolly blond-haired woman of middle age, with a cheerful grin. Usually wearing colorful bell-shaped skirts and carrying a wooden spoon.  

 Knows and greets about everyone by name, and is quick to ask a newcomer about themselves. She never forgets a face or name, and is friendly and talkative. She has no head for figures, however, and can be muddled with counting out a guests change, and can easily under, or overcharge him. Nor does she remember easily what items on her menu cost, and usually will ask someone else - even another "regular" customer. But her memory is flawless when it comes to news and people, and she is an excellent source of information.  

 Her older son Gavin is at the @[Carillon Tower](landmark:0723cf41-4ef8-46d2-baaf-7101f4146e4a).

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A two story building of stucco and half-timber, with a few translucent-glass windows on the first floor and a solid oak door. The sign hanging at the door is faded. One can barely make out the crossed lurs (horns) and the name of the tavern. Windows on the second floor overlook the streets.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The door opens into a comfortable common room, approximately 40' by 60', with beamed ceilings a plaster walls. The solid wood furniture looks well-used. Benches line the walls, along with old barrels that supplement the furniture on crowded nights. A small raised platform serves as a stage for impromptu entertainment. There is a bar and a fireplace along the inside wall, and a door that leads to the kitchen area. The rooms upstairs are for Ranna and her staff. Interior lighting is from sconces on the walls and two heavy iron chandeliers hanging from the ceiling.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
2:00pm - 12:00am

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair/Moderate

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Average

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
A small chest under counter contains [roll:1d6*5] in small change. At night all cash is secured in a heavy iron chest with a complexity 4 lock in a upstairs room.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
@[Ryan Campanella](person:42154ffa-8907-47d7-b5cb-29ea67fef792) - Ranna's youngest son, a red-haired, freckle faced boy of 14 who has the head for numbers Ranna lacks. He manages the business end of the Mixolydian Mode, occasionally chastising his mother for undercharging customers or spending too much. If Ryan leaves his usual post behind the counter, the cashbox goes with him. He is the only one who knows where the key to the iron chest is hidden. Ryan is not a musician, but he aspires to be a wealthy agent - he has a natural sales ability, and a quick wit. He's not into sharing gossip, however, and will get suspicious if asked too many leading questions. 

@[Nera](person:810c3471-1f82-4e31-80a1-aae2f8132c56) - A half-orc vagabond, a thin, bony girl of about 15, with dark shaggy hair and yellow eyes set aslant in her homely face. Taken in by Ranna, she cleans pots and pans in the kitchen and other simple chores. @[Nera](person:810c3471-1f82-4e31-80a1-aae2f8132c56) speaks common with a thick accent and is very shy around people, preferring to remain in the kitchen. Fiercely loyal to Ranna and Ryan, and dangerous with a thrown knife.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
Common room is 30% full until late evening (around 11:00 - 12:00 pm) when it can be very crowded indeed. Most customers are talking and drinking beer. Few eat here.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Gavin Campanella](person:ab9356b4-161e-4cb8-ba58-bf02cd209fc6) | @[Kruegger Rand](person:5c9dddff-792e-4a7f-aec6-92497f8d7a97) | @[Elias Thornapple](person:ad2da3f5-bfdf-45ab-8da6-dafc9400e306) | @[Phineous Tarkin](person:22ebacd4-69c7-4c04-ab9a-a87ddb31f2e4) | @[Robin O'Leary](person:a01786e8-604c-486c-8591-8716921489fe) | @[Largo Profundo](person:650522c3-ae93-4b5e-b2bb-43bd5ef14271) | @[Odino](person:0af121a6-59d5-4a1e-8617-598724b37469) the Nimble | @[Artemis Guisto](person:804ce8e0-190f-4321-982f-5c304ed4b844) | @[Amelia d'Larette](person:12cd58b5-6587-4b0a-9120-6ea19a9e9e5e) | @[Alfio Credenza](person:e95fe110-7ac2-4def-894a-539a3e0b78e9) | @[Florina](person:cad48790-4cf8-42b8-99bb-ec467e4bc642) | @[Magda Cordovan](person:f21efac9-a5f1-4ea5-bb6d-1f4f21172263) | @[Fenris Redbeard](person:b2213c6d-55d8-4ee8-afee-cb7865cb19eb) | @[Han Vilkorus](person:f2a4936a-f882-4761-b7ee-bd8b6d3c97ff) | @[Melisandre](person:3e36bdc2-4ec6-432d-b9bd-78ad5c800d64) | @[Luciano Clarino](person:2110a45a-d4b1-47c4-be2d-e35a52471a31)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Clientele are mostly local people, involved in performing in one form or another, and most know each other. Although not an unfriendly group, they are not likely to take up with strangers, unless they are also in "show business". Although there is a stage of sorts for entertainment, entertainment is rarely provided, except by the customers. A song thus presented would be new or different, not heard before. The primary interest of the customers is the beer, the food, and conversation, the favorite topics being happenings around town, and the people to whom it is happening.  

[h2]Rumors [/h2]
Rumors are rife at the Mixolydian Mode, since the traveling entertainers usually pick up a good deal of interesting tidbits of information, and then share them with their comrades over beer and cold mutton. Many rumors are personal anecdotes and just plain gossip, useless to player characters within and around Haven (unless their weird and enjoy knowing who is having an affair with whom, and where they are doing it, and so forth...). The GM is given these rumors as a guide to creating others, and to use as teasers to involve the players in the @[Scenarios](article:088e33cf-5a28-4c3f-bbe5-a243e610d2ff) in this and other sections.  

[ol]
[li]The unfortunate illness of Elarie Saspirando - she was unable to perform at that dinner party at the Berensten's. Her daughter is very worried. Algria Cambiata, her understudy, has been appearing for her and is doing very well. Rumor also has it that Algria is involved with Dominic Alderon, Elarie's former agent... 

[li]@[Fenris Redbeard](person:b2213c6d-55d8-4ee8-afee-cb7865cb19eb), the troubadour, is planning to take his troupe on the Road east to Mandalai (a city some 500 miles away) this spring but needs to hire some additional guards for the trip, (see "The Road Show" Adventure Opportunities, The South Corridor)

[li]There is a 10% chance that @[Rael Gavotte](person:1217ee33-13e6-4a14-8fdb-9755b8a993dc) is giving another one of his famous parties tonight. There will be wine from Karidda, and you know how Rael's parties are... (see NPC's, The South Corridor)

[li]General sympathies of the performers craft in the class struggle between Guild and Nobility lie with the merchants, who support the arts and are usually good tippers. 

[li]There is a gypsy girl on @[Trade Island](settlement:eec2fc60-5565-40fa-9047-69924589c400) that can sing like a true bard - she belongs in the Guild school, not living like a vagabond. What a waste of talent! (see "@[The Gypsy Nightingale](plot:32c13829-3219-4c4a-816e-9a30b1271d2e)", Trade Island)

[li]The new play at the Muses' Theater may never open - 'tis said the spirit of the mage that the play is about haunts Theater. Just last week, a stagehand was thrown bodily from the stage when no one was near him - and he remains in a semi-comatose state, as if bewitched. Nobody will enter Theater now... (see "Muses' Theater" The South Corridor)
[/ol]

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
The tavern that is the local "hangout" for bards, actors, etc. from the general neighborhood, and a hot spot for all kinds of news and gossip

articles.title: Mordecai - Surgeon
articles.content:
[h2]Sews up everything but broken hearts[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Mordecai](person:404a1f00-9cdb-46a7-8f04-5e492c8d7b2d) is short, round, balding, and has a sense of humor that considers slapping a sunburned man heartily on the back the height of hilarity. When he asks, "Now tell me if this hurts?" it generally will. He is extremely competent, and can usually save the worst sword wound (provided the patient is still alive when @[Mordecai](person:404a1f00-9cdb-46a7-8f04-5e492c8d7b2d) gets to work on him). He can restore HP up to half the patient's CON (those wounds received in a very recent - within the last two hours - fight), and has an 85% chance of saving the life of any character who has gone negative no deeper than his level. @[Mordecai](person:404a1f00-9cdb-46a7-8f04-5e492c8d7b2d) maintains his residence in a large two-story @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) house on Silk Veils. He claims he stays here because there are many duels in the area and he gets to treat lots of wounds (he likes to keep in practice). In the garden behind his house, he grows many herbs and plants that are used in various medicines. He is usually available day or night, although waking him out of a sound sleep causes him to double his fees.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair. @[Mordecai](person:404a1f00-9cdb-46a7-8f04-5e492c8d7b2d) gauges his fees both on the amount of time he has had to spend on the patient and the ability to pay. He is seldom exorbitant.
 
[h2]Quality[/h2]
One of the best surgeons in the @[Ten Cities](organization:0efc56fc-301e-4d3f-ba8c-019da1b01590).

articles.title: Mudikar's Saddlery and Tack Shop
articles.content:
[h2]Equipage for dressage - and even plain riding![/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Saddles, bridles, hackamores, and much more, are displayed over much of the main room of the shop. The quality is High, and prices are Costly, but good work and fine materials are not inexpensive. The lowest saddle cost is in the neighborhood of 75gp for a plain wrangler's working saddle, scaling up as ornamentation increases. 

Spells may be embedded on request (Mudikar has an arrangement with Enchantments, Ltd.), but the added costs are phenomenal. 

A custom made saddle, fitted to one's rump for ultimate comfort, costs about 400gp, and takes about six months to complete.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly

[h2]Quality[/h2]
High

articles.title: Muses' Theatre
articles.content:
[h2]Not really Mount Helicon[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Phineous Tarkin](person:22ebacd4-69c7-4c04-ab9a-a87ddb31f2e4) (see NPC's The South Corridor)

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A lovely Greek-styled building of marble and granite, with heavy bronze doors, fluted columns and an elaborate frieze on the eaves depicting nine young women in various poses and costume. A sign out front has a poster for the new play, "The Sorcerer's Secret", but the date has been scratched out and "coming soon" is written in over it.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
Theater has recently renovated and refurbished, at great expense. The floors are marble tile, the walls have niches with lovely statuary in them, there is new upholstery on the seats in Theater itself, and new curtains and drapes for the stage and boxes. The effect is of elegant opulence. The stage is set as a mage's workshop with books, a stuffed owl, a globe, humorous scrolls, a huge tome chained to a stand, wands, jars of mysterious substances, an ornate iron candelabra, a skull, a tall desk with parchment, pens and ink bottles, and a black cloak on a wall peg, to name a few items.  [br][br] There are dressing rooms and costume storage rooms backstage, and various other scenery and props.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
It isn't open

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
see Adventures, @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870)

[h2]Special Options[/h2]

articles.title: Music Copiers
articles.content:
[h2]@[Bennichio Lapiz](person:36906f0f-4f18-43cb-80b6-c95167a7d923), prop.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Bennichio Lapiz](person:36906f0f-4f18-43cb-80b6-c95167a7d923) is a plump, mild little man with thinning hair. His voice tends to squeak when excited, and usually deals with the customers.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
This building is rather nondescript, and the only indication of the shops presence is the small sign over the open door.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The front room of the shop has racks along the walls showing samples of the careful work of these specialized scribes.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
9:00am - 4:00pm

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
the cash box is kept in Bennichio's desk drawer. Trapped with a needle, save vs CON or sleep 8 hours. 3d10gp.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
The chief scribe, @[Farris](person:d465489a-6199-4166-91b8-1ed7b9cf8829), usually oversees the work and keeps the rowdy apprentices and journeymen under control and productive. @[Farris](person:d465489a-6199-4166-91b8-1ed7b9cf8829) is not above boxing a boy's ears for careless scribing or avoidable errors.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
There is a 40% chance of [roll:1d8] customers at any time with an additional 75% chance of an additional [roll:2d3] during lunch hours (11:30am - 1:00pm).

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
This shop puts out very high quality products, and is very well known, thus Bennichio does not feel he needs fancy (as well as expensive) frills. The shop is very Spartan, and little is wasted.

articles.title: Mustard and Fennel
articles.content:
[h2]We know herbalism![/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Fernlace runs the best herbalism shop in Haven and beyond. It is fully stocked and if she doesn't have it she can get it. 

On the second floor is a simply apartment where Fernlace and her apprentices live. The only things of monetary value present would be certain plants in the greenhouses out back.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
9:00am to 8:00pm

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair to Costly

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
There are two apprentices working in the shop: Red Oak is a young student herbalist showing great talent and Shagbark is an herbalist specializing in the geographic distribution of plants and is a great help in obtaining plants necessary to the work of advanced herbalists.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
At any time there will be [roll:1d4] customers in the shop given the location adjascent to the market.

articles.title: Mystic Valley Inn
articles.content:
[h2]A magical place to stay[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Bardol Murchisson](person:32facf49-fca0-43b3-83dd-75ea550ef436) retired from the practice of magic about ten years ago. He keeps his hand in, entertaining his customers in the evenings with small displays of prestidigitation and minor illusions. The inn has been part of the Haven cityscape for nearly two centuries, and Bardol inherited it from his father. He has no children of his own, and plans to will the establishment to the Mages Guild with the proviso that they keep it open to the public. He is tall and round (he likes good food and drink), with a wreath of white hair which flies wildly in all directions. He entrusts the running of the inn to @[Marjo](person:615ed882-b284-4c5d-9f95-80434c803a3e), a young man he hired for that purpose.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A large rambling wooden building which varies from 1 to 3 stories faces onto Caravan Street. There is a walled garden behind the main building, with a small cottage for the groundskeeper. Over the main door hangs a carved wooden sign with the words "Mystic Valley Inn", and a small picture of a pitcher pouring.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The main entrance leads directly to the common room, a large area filled with tables, chairs, benches, people, and pipe weed smoke. At the rear, a wide doorway leads to the kitchen, and a broad staircase leads upstairs to the lodging rooms. There is a bar, which glows, along the west wall of the common room, behind which is a rack of casks, barrels, and tuns. There are a number of small private rooms in the annex to the northwest of the main building.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
The inn accepts travelers at all hours. The tavern is open from 7:00am to 1:00am.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good. Quality food and drink, and outstanding entertainment in the evenings.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
A glowing stone coffer rests on one end of the bar. Unauthorized hands get fried touching it.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
@[Marjo](person:615ed882-b284-4c5d-9f95-80434c803a3e), the young man hired by Bardol to manage the inn, is a quality maitre d'hotel. He has improved the quality of the meals and service available, and it was he who originally suggested the evening displays of talent to Bardol. @[Marjo](person:615ed882-b284-4c5d-9f95-80434c803a3e) has hired sufficient additional personnel to provide good service for all the customers, and personally inspects the rooms and the kitchen daily.  

There are some 15 young girls who work as maids, bar girls, or serving wenches in the common room. In general, they are comely and well-mannered (discourtesy to a customer is grounds for dismissal), and will occasionally intercept a pass. 

The kitchen is manned by Numicia the Huge, a gigantic woman who is capable of giving a halfling chef an adequate contest in cooking.  

A number of years ago, a deaf-mute (who was eventually named William) appeared mysteriously at the inn. He now resides in the groundskeeper's cottage, and makes it his business to keep the garden clean and beautiful. He has a green thumb that is the envy of many herbalists in the city.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
There are usually 120 to 200 people in the common room at almost any hour. The chances for a vacant room are about 80% before 7:00pm, 50% from 7:00 to 9:00, and 20% after 9:00.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
Assorted magicians make the inn a hangout, and there are usually 1d10 [roll:1d10] bending an elbow with a mug of brew at any given time.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
The tavern is frequented by many of Bardol's compatriots from his days of magic, and there are generally two or three arcanists willing to put on displays of one sort or another for an evening's entertainment.

articles.title: Nimrodel's South City Shipyard
articles.content:
[h2]Shipbuilding and repair[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The shipyard is a large, walled complex, with ways for building and dry-dock repair for three ships. This is the first yard that @[Nimrodel](person:c23b1ec6-6ac7-4c88-bff2-ef81a0a78957) started with over 150 years ago, and he still maintains his primary offices here. He owns three other yards. One upriver, and two downriver, outside the walls, for major new building. Except for the office in one corner of the yard, the rest of the large yard is covered with scattered sheds and roofed over areas for the storage of spars, masts, lumber, kegs of pitch, etc. for shipbuilding. There are gates to the yard on both Warehouse Row and Drayer's Loop, which are locked at night, and patrolled by six private guards. 

 @[Nimrodel](person:c23b1ec6-6ac7-4c88-bff2-ef81a0a78957) employs nearly 100 laborers in his shipyard, involved in carpentry, ship fittings, and other similar skills. There are also a number of clerks, and ship designers. There is only a 5% chance of a job opening for qualified men, as @[Nimrodel](person:c23b1ec6-6ac7-4c88-bff2-ef81a0a78957) is known as a fair and honest man, and men rarely leave his employ once hired on. @[Nimrodel](person:c23b1ec6-6ac7-4c88-bff2-ef81a0a78957) himself does little save design work. And leaves most of the running of the yard to his son @[Perendhil](person:70123c0c-fdb7-4d8f-89f8-045fd8338bbc), and the foreman, @[Hanson Frigate](person:d22424c3-e23c-4dbe-81a2-af9c8c26db7d). 

 At present, two of the three ways are occupied. One is a new vessel, little more than a skeleton hull, and the other is one of the city's galleys, Dorian Queen, in dry-dock for minor refitting, including a new rudder.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Perendhil](person:70123c0c-fdb7-4d8f-89f8-045fd8338bbc) | @[Hanson Frigate](person:d22424c3-e23c-4dbe-81a2-af9c8c26db7d) | @[Raf Poul](person:ebb79257-ab7d-4687-939a-9ae828fea67f)

articles.title: No-Yen Drachmah - Goldsmith
articles.content:
[h2]Money lent, collateral accepted[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
No-Yen lends money to major businessmen in the city, and to very well-known out-of-towners. No-Yen's office is on the first level of his home in @[Gold Alley](landmark:126c954d-648d-488e-a7d5-5c9f436c95df), and he is generally available from 1:00pm 'til 8:00pm daily. His interest rates are reasonable (only 5% per month, compounded). He will loan up to 1,000gp to known borrowers with no collateral, and make maximum loans of 10,000gp with proper collateral. He has two Goliath "enforcers" who go out to collect overdue loans. They seldom have problems in collecting, either money or collateral. The two Goliaths are Kuori "Longleaper" Anakalathia and Vimak "Steadyhand" Anakalathia. They are brothers who were exiled from Krindor for attempted robbery.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Kuori Anakalathia](person:4905dd01-c5aa-429a-9304-7446ee5201ed) | @[Vimak Anakalathia](person:876e45db-621d-469e-aa75-4b7fc1fbabb2)

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
No-Yen may decide to make loans to player characters that have some sort of collateral to offer (magic items, property rights, etc.). This requires a saving roll against CHA in addition to collateral. There is a limit of 5,000gp on a first loan to an unknown, regardless of the amount of collateral.

articles.title: Numirolakos the Gentler
articles.content:
[h2]Training of mounts by centaurs[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Legend has it that a centaur trained horse will only throw a cruel master. Certainly the rapport achieved by centaur and horse makes the training sessions much easier and quicker, and it may be that there is actual communication in some language unknown to members of the biped races, for horses "educated" by centaur trainers are the gentlest and most cooperative mounts to be found.  

 @[Numirolakos](person:d063adbd-f0b6-4c27-a2b5-cc4d874016e9) is probably the best known of the assorted horse training establishments in the Market. It is the only one which exclusively employs centaurs. The basic training course for equines at the school lasts for three months. At that time, the mount is introduced to its prospective rider, and a one month acclimation period begins, after which the steed will usually (95%) accept no other rider. 

The regular fee at the school is 500gp to train a horse to basic standards. The fees go up exponentially for "the fancy stuff" (coming when called, battle training, protecting one's master, etc.).

[h2]Staff[/h2]
All trainers are centaurs

articles.title: Odino's Dance and Tumbling
articles.content:
[h2]@[Odino](person:0af121a6-59d5-4a1e-8617-598724b37469) of Mandalai[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The entire first floor is one large room. Mats are stacked neatly along a wall when not in use, and racks of barbells, ropes, etc. line the other wall. A door against the back wall leads to stairs going up and down. Downstairs, there is a food storage area and a large bath and sauna. Upstairs are @[Odino](person:0af121a6-59d5-4a1e-8617-598724b37469)'s rooms, which are starkly furnished, and a small shrine to Eollana.  

 @[Odino](person:0af121a6-59d5-4a1e-8617-598724b37469) is a small, dark, wiry fellow, full of nervous energy. He teaches tumbling to students with at least an average DEX for 5gp a week for daily 2 hour sessions. @[Odino](person:0af121a6-59d5-4a1e-8617-598724b37469) is a good teacher, and if a student does well (STA INT and DEX), after 3 months, can improve coordination and reflexes (d6: 1-3 +1, 4-5 +2, 6 +3). @[Odino](person:0af121a6-59d5-4a1e-8617-598724b37469) is into a "health food" diet of brown rice and raw vegetables, which he eagerly espouses to his students, along with meditation sessions and a regular exercise ritual. The improvement will last as long as the student keeps up the half-hour of exercise ritual daily.  

 @[Odino](person:0af121a6-59d5-4a1e-8617-598724b37469) has little money. Other than necessities, it is believed he takes the bulk of his money to the Temple of Eollana.

articles.title: Othmar the Astrologer
articles.content:
[h2]Readings from the stars[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Othmar](person:4e81a5ac-1711-4170-a1c0-eeec3041aac3) is about 50 years old, with a gray, wispy beard and mustache, and a raspy voice. A virtual recluse, little has been done in the matter of his personal hygiene for a long period - his body and the disheveled blue robe he constantly wears appear to have never been washed in the last ten years, and he constantly scratches himself. @[Othmar](person:4e81a5ac-1711-4170-a1c0-eeec3041aac3) tells a good story when he gives a reading, and he always puts his predictions in the most optimistic context. As a result, he has developed a faithful clientele, despite his personal habits.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
There is a sign in the front window of the second floor of the Scribe service, showing a moon and stars pattern, against a bright yellow background.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
At the top of a flight of stairs, off the hall to the Scribe's office, is a locked door with a huge brass doorknocker. The consultation room reeks of incense and sour sweat. Astrological books and star charts are strewn about the area, and overflow the two crude wooden bookcases against a side wall. The @[Astrologer](person:b58b4d7a-d4c8-42dd-92ac-58e6007fb988) conducts his readings at a small circular table in the middle of the room. Four chairs surround it, and a guttering oil lamp and a smoking incense burner complete the setting.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
Noon to Midnight.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly. Immediate future readings run from 3gp to 7gp, with full-life readings ranging from 25gp to 50gp. Tarot readings may be performed for 10gp to 25gp. Price quotes vary depending on @[Othmar](person:4e81a5ac-1711-4170-a1c0-eeec3041aac3)'s estimate of the sucker's...ah, client's ability to pay.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good. @[Othmar](person:4e81a5ac-1711-4170-a1c0-eeec3041aac3) provides very acceptable predictions, even if they seldom come true.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
There is some 800gp in coin wrapped in a dark piece of cloth, and stashed inside @[Othmar](person:4e81a5ac-1711-4170-a1c0-eeec3041aac3)'s straw mattress (in the back area, behind the curtain).

[h2]Staff[/h2]
This is strictly a one-man operation.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
There is a 15% chance [roll:1d100] that @[Othmar](person:4e81a5ac-1711-4170-a1c0-eeec3041aac3) is engaged in a reading. If so, he will gruffly tell all visitors to "come back later. I'm extremely busy!"

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Mathilde Hochritter](person:73dc6f37-7bc6-44e5-855c-981da5ad4ed2) | @[Talia Blackbourne](person:d22a645f-1c2d-4f6e-a34b-8d7de35cb961) | @[Gilberto Maggia](person:f8abcaf4-8f94-42f6-84ea-94c3c8c1b1a4) | @[Claudia de la Riis](person:646e36a4-cc41-4a91-8076-5af2dcb007fb) | @[Antonio Berensten](person:ec8f50d3-84f6-48a6-95d0-d7d6b5b65cb8) | @[Joffa the Barakite](person:418c5698-ce79-4a43-930d-c520ee28b4bb)

articles.title: Otto Chubb - Butcher
articles.content:
[h2]Cuts O' Meat[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Otto Chubb](person:898f4536-cf08-4ecf-8fec-85997c07751b)'s store offers meat on the hoof in more ways than one these days. While roly-poly Otto and his equally rotund wife Ingrid dispense cuts of meat, and trade tales and gossip with their customers, his daughter Bundy lounges around the front of the shop, hungrily eying the male customers that pass through.  

 Unbeknownst to her parents, Bundy has gotten herself in the "family way", and is desperately searching for a male halfling willing to be her husband. She is quite comely of face and form (though looking at her parents, one could justifiably have doubts about how long her svelteness will last). And would make a good homemaker.  

 Since Otto knows nothing of Bundy's past indiscretion, and Bundy does not have the nerve to tell her father the truth, anyone associating with Bundy socially now runs the risk of being railroaded onto a crossbow wedding when her condition becomes more obvious.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Bundy Chubb](person:012c4d09-2f73-45ed-a444-3aedeb3ab89c)

articles.title: Petals of the Rose
articles.content:
[h2]House of Seaman's Delights[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
A brothel modeled loosely on the more elaborate establishments on @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c), it is, however, generally referred to by the local permanent residents as the "Scales of the Fish". The owner, @[Madame Dorilla](person:9fc39a04-6ef7-4535-945d-dcfd8c2efb36), was once a very popular courtesan on @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c). Now she is tired, middle-aged, and disillusioned, and was easy prey for @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60)'s extortionists, who collect a sizable portion of the money brought in by the Rose's dozen or so girls as "insurance".

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Moonlight](person:86d6a078-d3c3-4d08-aa2d-25a4c7a077eb)

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
One of the girls, a sharp-witted half-elf named @[Moonlight](person:86d6a078-d3c3-4d08-aa2d-25a4c7a077eb), has managed to discover unusual information (see @[Scenarios](article:088e33cf-5a28-4c3f-bbe5-a243e610d2ff): Rescue by Moonlight). She has not yet acted on this information, since she has no way to escape @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60)'s certain and deadly revenge.

articles.title: Pickett 'Lefty' Post - Merchandise
articles.content:
Lefty (he is missing his right hand at the wrist courtesy of Haven's justice and Lefty's one mistake as a burglar) deals in a plethora of different items. He knows some types of merchandise (particularly jewelry and metalwork) quite well, and has at least a nodding acquaintance with most others. 

There is a quite reasonable chance (60%) of finding most small merchandise items among Lefty's stock, but only a 35% chance for large items (rugs, furniture, etc.). The assistant, Migul, helps with customers during the day, but is seldom present in the evenings.

Lefty operates as a fence for smaller stolen items. His ratings as a fence are:
- Up to 15k gp value at any one time
- Fields: jewelry, silver, complex mechanics
- For items outside his fields: 65% value on small items, 15% on large
- Min/Max offers: 10%/45% of value; 5%/30% if obviously "hot"
[br]
Most of his illicit dealings are conducted after dark so Lefty is one of the few in the Market who does not shut down at dusk or shortly thereafter. 

Robbery attempts have been made on Lefty and his stock, and one or two have actually succeeded. In most cases, however, the local thieves and pickpockets have acted to protect their source of money and various would-be robbers have been found dead, handless, or nailed to walls in the vicinity of Thieves' Market. No Guild thief will touch Lefty and attempts at robbery have nearly always been by unaligned out-of-towners.

articles.content:
[h2]Items of every kind sold[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Bozulouski Piringolli](person:ea1ef21c-0d2d-4533-a00d-ed5bc373c337) runs an emporium which boasts it carries the city's largest supply of everything. This is, of course, pure exaggeration, but the store does have a Very Wide selection of most household items in regular demand. These are sold at prices Cheap to Fair. The shop opens at 9am sharp every day, and closes when Piringolli boots the last customer out (usually about 7:30 in the evening).

9:00am - 7:30pm

Cheap to Fair
