articles.title: Pocheffski's School of Arms
articles.content:
[h2]Fighting for felons[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Pocheffski](person:d2ee2ac9-3cd6-4dab-8103-0c1ce7265a52), a sallow-faced, squint-eyed man in his late fifties whose reflexes are still cat-quick despite the toll of advancing years on his vision is the Thieves Guild's Weapons Master. Of all the Guild's former inner circle (save @[Azimuth](person:38b3505c-7430-4028-8042-c9ce2756fab1), of course), he has perhaps lost the most in the fire's aftermath. 

His "school" on Porcupine Alley is little more than an empty warehouse outfitted with a few ropes, tumbling mats, and sandbags, and he deeply mourns the loss of all the high-priced training equipment (the rough terrain and nighttime simulation areas, and the immense mechanized climbing apparatus) that populated his domain in Rogues' Roost. More significantly, @[Pocheffski](person:d2ee2ac9-3cd6-4dab-8103-0c1ce7265a52) is no longer permitted direct access to the Guild's armory of specialized and enhanced weaponry, and may only request such items through the auspices of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) chapter's Master @[Jurgan Bland](person:3f3117f4-fc70-4e98-bfd5-525c4c168bb6) (an old crony of Duur's). 

Although these slights have made @[Pocheffski](person:d2ee2ac9-3cd6-4dab-8103-0c1ce7265a52) somewhat desultory about his teaching duties, he remains one of the truly expert authorities on the use of exotic weaponry (including garrotes, blowguns, and really unusual items like nunchaku) in the @[Ten Cities](organization:0efc56fc-301e-4d3f-ba8c-019da1b01590) region. He maintains a small arsenal of such devices in the one-story flat he keeps as his residence.

articles.content:
[h2]One man struggling to survive in the corpse of his failed business[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Refer to Twisted Taverns, page 87[br] F:\Bob's Stuff\SkyDrive\Gaming\Twisted Taverns\The Seeker' s Guide to Twisted Taverns.pdf

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Just Larry since his wife died, his sons left (or were imprisoned) and young daughter Luna was taken.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
Engog is a young half-orc (use the bandit stat block) who occasionally visits Poor Larrys because of the cheap grog. He wears an open waistcoat and simple pants, the same clothes he wears while working in the fields.

Kai Brownsmith is a red-haired human woman (commoner) in her late 20s, and the daughter of a coppersmith in town. She wears common clothes covered in patches from burns during casting.

Gastroe Oakenclub  is a dwarven drunkard and veteran who regularly drinks beyond his limits and makes a mess in Poor Larry’s. He occasionally brings in old drinking buddies to overturn the entire dining area.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
As many as 12 guests [roll:2d6] can typically be found nursing their drinks, some quietly washing away sorrows and others energetically laughing at Larry. Most interactions with them involve complaints about service speed and the blandness of the food or drinks.

articles.title: Professor's Challenge
articles.content:
[h2]Coffee House and games[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Theadus McKessin](person:3e162b2b-4360-4c3e-96a7-1a129fcdffeb)

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A quaint red @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) building of one level has a sign displaying a silver armored knight on the back of a griffin outside its door.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
A large front room makes up the whole shop. There are old wooden tables and chairs, some booths, and a counter area. The shop seats 30 people. Anybody making the slightest noise within the shop front will receive a chorus of "shhhh!!" and very cold stares from the customers.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
10:00am to 10:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good, if Theadus makes the coffee (35%) and poor if any other clerk makes it (65%).

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
A wooden box is in the only back room, where the coffee is stored. It has a Complexity 2 lock and contains [roll:1d4] x 1d6gp in assorted small coins.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Theadus, an old elf, works in the store on weekends and his two counter clerks @[Murfy](person:6c8b169b-7538-4da0-b039-eefb9554fd6f) and @[Giblet](person:a59301e8-1170-4628-abba-762039979296) work during the week. Theadus is a teacher at the College of Alchemy, the bungling professor type with spectacles and a nose-tuned voice box. He is the only surviving member of the Strathspey Regiment.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
At any particular time, there will be [roll:1d4*2] customers in pairs playing Haven's equivalent to chess. On Firesday (just before the weekend) the store will have [roll:1d6*1d5] customers, with the odd ones looking for a good game at a good bet (watch it! - most of these old guys know their stuff).

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Most of the tables have chess boards on them. Pieces may be acquired from the counter clerk.

articles.title: Queen Takes Pawn
articles.content:
[h2]Pawning Business[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Regin A'Queen](person:90f261b7-8577-4c03-91e2-66f582e102ce) - is a half-elf with an eye for trinkets. He is new in Haven and, as a result, habitually gets lost in the labyrinthine side streets every weekend. (His greatest dream is to accumulate enough money to visit his homeland some thousand miles north of Haven).

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A shop with a many-faceted window faces Lorien Street, an alley on the east side of the building leads to a back road. On the shop's window is a translucent painting showing a queen ordering the execution of a convict ("Innocent!" asserts Regin).

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The front room is filled with ceiling high piles of boxes, each containing myriad objects. The piles are arranged in a maze, around which a perilous path (menaced by swaying stacks which threaten to topple momentarily) meanders through the cluttered room. Magical light continually floods the areas so that search is possible without carrying artificial sources. Each week, the piles change and the boxes move - Regin must keep mental track of his inventory, and he has a lot of it. Virtually anything a player might want is available here, if s/he is willing to spend the time to search (don't take it from the bottom!!).

[h2]Hours[/h2]
10:00am to 5:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Depending on Reg's mood he will charge from .5 to 1.5 times the worth of any particular item - [(3 + 2d6)/10]%.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
GM's discretion (Remember, what is at the bottom of a stack, ain't necessarily what's oldest).

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Located under a hidden desk near the front door is a strong box of steel with a Complexity 3 lock. It contains [roll:1d10] x 1d10gp in mixed coins and small gems, and Regin's ledgers.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
Besides the occasional customer, only Regin is found in the shop, usually reading or taking inventory on new items. He is quite a talker when he strikes up a conversation. 

At the start of the week there is a 65% chance that he has become lost over the weekend and the store is closed, a sign will be posted on the front window reading, "Back soon, hopefully!"

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
The GM should restock the store once per month with 1d6special items. Presently there are two valuables which may be found (10% chance cumulative to locate per hour of search). The first is a hand-painted deck of Tarot cards wrapped in a black silk cloth. The cards are in mint condition, priced at 2,000gp. The second is a dusty old book with a cover lock (Complexity 6). The book is a treatise on demonology, complete with a spell to summon Balrogim (it doesn't say how to banish them, though, nor how to control them) - use of this manual (actually, survival from the fire demon likely to appear) grants an additional 2d12 x 100 EP to a demonologist or mage of any type. It is priced at 35gp.

articles.title: Rackley's Museum of Oddities
articles.content:
[h2]If it's weird, they have it[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Bensoaman Rackley](person:0decf390-0920-4391-9e4a-d70beca4a827) is an unusual man, 7' 6" tall, with arms that almost touch the floor, and a very round and completely hairless head with lavender eyes and large (almost elephantine) ears (which wiggle!), who runs an unusual business. His museum of oddities is just that. The exhibits he displays include such things as the three-headed baby, a stuffed hippogator, Mogacoran the Mage (who lost an arcane battle to Cu'uga the Accursed, and will probably stand for eternity with the same stupid expression on his face), and the smallest pegasus in captivity (about 2' high, with a 6' wingspread - it seems to have gotten in the way of a shrinking spell). Many people pass through his establishment in the course of a day - the fee is only 2sp - and never fail to be astounded and amused (or in some cases, disgusted and angered) by the exhibits there.  

 Bensoaman Is always looking for new oddities to display in his halls, and will usually pay well for a true oddity. He will even let groups use one of the many maps or charts he has accumulated, in search of new and wondrous things he can display. He is not interested in the treasure the group might find, just the truly unusual. Of the 346 maps and charts he owns, there are 35 (a 10% chance) which lead to actual treasures. Of the rest, 173 (50%) are totally worthless fakes, 69 (20%) have already been sacked by one group of adventurers or another, and the rest are nearly Impossible to read or have some important piece missing.

articles.title: Ralki - Men's Tailor
articles.content:
[h2]Fine Tailored Products[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Ralki](person:2c4d43b1-b3fd-415d-8b88-306af9a7386d)'s establishment is like day compared to @[Jambur](person:8e95192f-5952-4630-b6a0-baf8deec903b)'s night. @[Ralki](person:2c4d43b1-b3fd-415d-8b88-306af9a7386d) is a very diminutive, elderly dwarf with horn-rimmed spectacles, and a military posture. He does only custom tailoring (waiting time, from first fitting to receipt, ranges from 10-28 days) and has an uncannily precise sense of fit. He serves all races with equal skill (Ralki is so good he can make a halfling look like a Swiss banker).  

 His clientele includes several of the major Guild families, and - though this is a very well-kept secret - is occasionally called to Duke Fernando's estate to fit him for formal attire. @[Hamlin Blackbourne](person:24dec529-0265-4bb9-bb8c-d6240dea4bb9) (Guild of the Loom's Master) has long tried to get @[Ralki](person:2c4d43b1-b3fd-415d-8b88-306af9a7386d) to work for him, but the latter prizes his independence too highly ("De only time I took orders from anyvun, vas during de last Goblin-Dvarf var - and dat vas qvite enough, tank you").  

 A character dressed in one of @[Ralki](person:2c4d43b1-b3fd-415d-8b88-306af9a7386d)'s outfits should probably receive temporary bonuses of +1 to +3 in CHA if he is in a position where a person's attire would be important to his image (like an explorer asking a possible benefactor for financial assistance, or a male-female relationship in the upper social strata).

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Superb+

articles.title: Red Nick's Tavern
articles.content:
[h2]Hangout of the Longshoremen[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The tavern is in two old row houses on a back alley, not far from the docks. The place is far from fancy, and the quality of the beer varies tremendously, but it's cheap. The tavern is run by @[Red Nick](person:4de604fc-1bee-458e-b241-dd120f4a8053), who spends most of his time sitting around the bar, drinking from his private stock. He leaves the serving of the regular ale and a peppery stew to the cook, @[Maggie](person:9dc5c5ee-90f7-4e4a-bcb3-d882685c5130). The normal customers are dockside laborers, drayers, and longshoremen, a rough and ready crowd, as the worn and mended furnishings will attest. 

 Nick's real business is not the bar, but a fencing operation in stolen and smuggled magic items. The bar serves as a cover for this highly profitable, but dangerous trade. He is a careful man, and will only deal with people he knows, or those who have some sort of good references. He often sells his merchandise to Alphonso Caradello, a member of the smuggling arm of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60), although Nick himself is not a member of the Hand.

articles.title: Residence of Rigaletto and Paladin Brandybuck
articles.content:
[h2]Where @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515)'s most prominent citizens entertain the city's elite[/h2]

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A flagstone pathway leads off from Hillandale Street, and splits in two at the base of the hill. The segments lead to two elaborately carved cherry wood doors, 80 feet apart. The left hand door is engraved with the emblem of a mace held in a black leather glove, and the right hand door with a mercantile insignia. Only the face of the smial, and its living room, can be seen from street level.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The house is organized into two completely and elaborately finished apartments occupied by Paladin and Rigaletto, respectively. At the center of the houses, the inner doors can be swung back to form a communal party room.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Paladin sleeps with his money under his pillow. Rigaletto has a wall safe in his study with a complexity level 7 lock.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
In addition to the Brandybucks, an elderly halfling woman named Lissa Glass serves as housekeeper for the two men and lives on the premises. A chef named Ambo is called in to prepare the food for their frequent parties, Paladin, because of his Guard duties, will be absent from home several nights each week.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Rigaletto Brandybuck](person:53057cb8-e5cd-4c05-a98d-af9b1265a974) & @[Paladin Brandybuck](person:a8dfde5b-106c-4fa0-be8b-c5182a691896) hold fairly large (12-30 person) dinner parties about once a month. The guest lists at these affairs are comprised almost totally (80-95%) of influential merchants from the Corridor, members of the Guild leadership, or key figures in the elven and dwarven communities.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Paladin has, among his personal effects, the stuffed heads of several wild beasts (bagged in the dark wilds of the local taxidermist), a collection of cloth-bound volumes on military history, and a huge bronze statue of a halfling warrior in full fighting pose. Rigaletto of course has an expensive wardrobe of silks and velvets, and a number of beautiful masterworks culled from his shop over the years. He also owns an obsidian and jade chess set, and has a map of Haven and its surrounding territories that fills an entire wall of his study.

articles.title: Residence of Rombo Alecastle
articles.content:
[h2]Home for an aging adventurer[/h2]

[h2]Interior[/h2]
Those few who are invited to visit the now reclusive former adventurer are treated with warm hospitality, and a chance to browse among the many mementos of Rombo's wanderings. 

In the study, there are piles of parchment and bound diaries strewn about the long table where Rombo's young associate, @[Chelsea Cheddar](person:64d30f65-3200-4edd-b715-ae5696d180d9), works editing the former's memoirs. 

In a sunny alcove of the front room, Rambo works at his current pastime of cartography, detailing many of the areas of his travels from memory (still excellent, despite his advancing years). 

Among his treasures are a Ring of Flying and a large chunk of feldspar with a Find Direction spell embedded in it, both (among other items) are kept in several immaculately clean glass cases linked to alarms. 

Rombo has a secret passage in the dressing closet of his bedroom that leads to the underground levels of @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954), for he is much loved by the dwarven peoples for his years of service.

articles.title: Rocky's Tavern and Arena
articles.content:
[h2]Bets and gaming[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
A one story house with a walled-in yard in back, the yard is set up as an arena, with a large pit 5' deep and 25' square, and benches around all sides. A grimy, torn canvas tent encloses the arena and seating area, with the only entrance being through the pub. 

 @[Rocky](person:d9772e20-3fac-4d00-94b3-38a54cbc655f), a big, scarred, potato-faced ex-fighter, runs the tavern and the arena, which features numerous two-bit boxers, gladiators, and cock- or dogfights several nights a week. The sports are bloody and brutal, and involve a good bit of betting (from which the house takes a reasonable cut) and much beer and ale, as well as an admittance fee. The fighters receive a small percentage of the admittance fee, with winners receiving a purse of around 50 GP.

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
Fighting cocks should be rated at the beginning of their careers for HP (2d6 + 8, for arena purposes only), DEX (2d5 + 8), and CON (3d6). Combat rounds are 1 second long. Each round make a saving roll against DEX for each cock. If successful, a point of damage has been scored on the opposing cock. If the roll is successfully made, and is less than half of DEX, damage scored is doubled - if it is missed by more than half the cock's DEX, his opponent scores an extra point of damage. These fights are usually to the death, although the owner of a cock may stop the fight (admitting defeat for his bird in the process) if he feels the cock is worth saving. It is neither impossible nor unlikely for both cocks to be killed in the fight. Cocks recover damage at the rate of 1/5 CON per day; 1/4 of the cock's total experience (see below) is additionally healed on the first day. [br][br] Each time a cock wins a fight, it gains 1 point of experience. If it kills its opponent while sustaining less than half its HP in damage, it gains 2 experience points. These may be added to HP (1HP for 2EP) or to DEX (1 point for 3EP). Cocks start fighting at about 6 months of age, and seldom live beyond 60 months. Their fighting prime ends at about 30 months of age, and a saving roll against 1/2 DEX is required monthly after this to avoid the loss of a point of DEX; 1 point is lost automatically every 4 months in any case. [br][br] @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) is a reasonably fertile source of fighting cocks. The inhabitants frequently care more for their birds than for their children. Two of the larger cock breeder/trainers in the area are Nelido Silver- thumb and Benno the Crab (a bent and gnarled little man with a peculiar way of walking sidewise). Both are frequently in attendance at @[Rocky](person:d9772e20-3fac-4d00-94b3-38a54cbc655f)'s, and are happy to sell birds to those wishing to buy - a good bird (reroll any HP or DEX result of 13 or less) will normally cost about 250 GP.

articles.title: Rose Garden Inn
articles.content:
[h2]Disrespect the rose and you shall reap the thorns[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
For a full descriptions refer to Glorious Taverns, page 138.

The "Baroness" is a no-nonsense elf who runs the inn with militaristic discipline. Her main objective is to keep her business lucrative and catering to only the most successful of upper nobility and their distinguished guests. She has neither the time nor tolerance for mistakes or half measures. Her countenance is stoically beautiful, and she speaks firmly and directly while very rarely engaging in small talk. She bears a cold and direct presence that is felt tenfold by those in her employ.

Formerly a lord’s mansion, The Rose Garden Inn prides itself as being the finest establishment not only within the city walls, but the entire region. The lush and vibrant gardens and promenades that grace the perimeter of the mansion were once open to the public, until its sturdy perimeter fence was built some time ago. Now, with the enclosure, these aromatic alcoves, gardens and scenic walks are available to guests and their visitors only.

Overall, the Rose Garden Inn boasts an atmosphere that is quite lavish and pretentious. In the daylight hours, the numerous flower gardens and elegant walkways serve as a means of afternoon tea, or a chance for couples in potential courtship to promenade. The ornate banquet hall also lends itself to such opportunities for those guests who do not wish to spend time in the sunlight and enjoy conversations undisturbed by the noise of the city or its harbors. Often these conversations involve business of high importance. In fact, some of the largest export deals in existence have been struck within the inn’s walls.

As is evident throughout the entire location, only the finest furniture and furnishings have been selected for The Rose Garden Inn. The bedrooms are spacious, with large beds whose posts are worked with carvings and inlaid with silver. Elegant silken sheets are provided daily. Every bedroom is laid with thick red carpets. Lavish stone baths are located separately from the bedrooms, with the exception of the penthouse, which includes personal baths. Staff members place fresh flowers in decorative ceramic vases and replace them daily. Selections of wine are also  included in the bedrooms.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
[aloud]
Just inside Shield Gate you see a marvellous three-tiered structure of polished @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) peeking above the other buildings you first negotiate a sturdy iron perimeter fence. Following this, you come to a stone archway that is wrapped in rich green ivy and through which you see a luscious green lawn. The smell of the freshly cut grass fills the senses. 

A cobbled road leads the way to the main stone stairwell of the mansion and is ornamented with flower gardens and flowing granite fountains. The tavern stable hands are busy and bustling as they help patrons disembark. You can feel the heaviness of the rich history that is associated with this old establishment and swells of anticipation race as you get closer to the heavy ornate exotic hardwood door which through its glass panels you can distinctly see blurs of activity.
[/aloud]

The exterior of the establishment is comprised mainly of polished @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3). It is window-laden, with each glass panel bearing intricate ironmongery. A three-story marvel, a tall archway of ivy-wreathed stone serves as the entrance onto the main lawn. Down the center of the lawn traverses a smooth cobble path that diverges into the various flower beds and hedgerows that ornament this portion of the property. This road leads right up to the front stairwell of the Rose Garden Inn, up which a heavy ornate door of exotic hardwood and glass panels leads guests within.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
[aloud]
Upon entry, you find a grand staircase directly in the center of the main hall. This leads up to the second floor of the property, where one will find accommodations situated. To the left and right of the main entrance are subsidiary walkways leading to various ball rooms, smoking rooms, studies and dining halls.
[/aloud]

One of the establishment’s twenty-two employees will provide guests with a tour of the mansion, as it is common for one to get lost among its various corridors and rooms.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Expensive

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent

[h2]Staff[/h2]
22 staff work the Inn as servers, cooks, maids, etc.   In addition there are always four burley security staff on duty at any time, day or night.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
@[Ephi](person:b40ed481-4d9e-4352-a83c-f0208d598867) has lived among the patrons at The Rose Garden Inn longer than she can remember. After turning herself invisible one day, she followed a carriage through the main gate, and its company through the main doors.

From that point forward, she has magically disguised herself by altering her appearance into a near-carbon copy of the inn’s guests—or more specifically, their children. Occasionally she will take on the appearance of a chaste human female in search of courtship and dazzle in the ballroom; at others that of a distinguished gentleman so as to lounge in the smoking room. Hers is a genuine, insatiable thirst for innocent mischief. She particularly enjoys confounding guests to the point of utter bewilderment

@[Reliddack Wulviss](person:da5f050c-fa5c-44f4-8d84-4f72a7e130ae) is a jovial, older gnome with an engaging personality and sharp wit. His congenial nature and small stature make him well-liked, especially amongst children. Reliddack is known for growing thriving medicinal herbs, such as can cure even diseases heretofore believed incurable. Additionally, he has found cures for other, more aesthetic, afflictions, such as the appearance of old age. His access to such properties has gained him significant ground in the highest of social circles.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
Any outsiders who arrive to visit guests must do so by invitation only. Those without proper invitation are turned away by the rotating quartet of guardsmen that are on duty around the clock.

articles.title: Ruin of Rogues' Roost
articles.content:
[h2]The former citadel of crime[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
A burned-out shell of what was once a large warehouse, only part of the walls are left standing, and the lot is filled with rubble. In fact, there is little more than rubble left along almost the entire street, as the fire spread throughout the west side of Cust Way. This was the former headquarters of the Thieves Guild, burned down in a daring raid by @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60) six months ago. Some say (though not too loudly in this part of town) that the power of the Guild, symbolized by the Roost, may be permanently on the wane.

articles.title: Sakbar - Excavation Contractor
articles.content:
[h2]Construction and Excavation[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Sakbar](person:6c7899a8-6d84-4d6e-98a2-f810ea211e9c) employs about three score working class dwarves and hires them out for pick and shovel work (ditch digging, demolition, etc.) He himself a reasonably competent stone mason, and with three other assistants will also take on small construction jobs (homes, small footbridges, and the like). Within the city limits, his workmen keep their noses clean. But on jobs outside the jurisdiction of the Guilds, @[Sakbar](person:6c7899a8-6d84-4d6e-98a2-f810ea211e9c)'s crews will often walk off the job at a critical juncture in its completion, using any small incident as a pretext for declaring the site unsafe or the land owner unreasonable. They will then demand higher wages and benefits to complete the project. @[Sakbar](person:6c7899a8-6d84-4d6e-98a2-f810ea211e9c)'s reputation for these hold-up tactics is well known around Haven, if anyone bothers to ask around. Otherwise, Caveat Emptor!

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair/High

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair

articles.content:
[h2]A writer's ability without the cramp[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Culver Trask](person:d7e4f66b-7c4e-47c3-8103-0416fb30acc2) and Janus Domenici Trask a husband-and-wife team, endeavor to provide decent service for the nobles of @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b). He is a tall middle-aged merchant with hair still jet black, and piercing gray eyes. Possessed of a humble self-image, he is genuinely grateful for his modest business successes, and strives to provide rapid service for his customers (he will make urgent or private personal deliveries himself, and can be trusted to keep a confidence - except from his wife, whom he worships completely). Janus is the daughter of Pietro Domenici, a local ship's captain and explorer of some small renown, who was lost at sea when she was a young woman. She is still a striking woman with hip length auburn hair and greenish eyes, but the years of indoor labor have left her pale and wan, and she seems to have forgotten how to smile. She will not travel by water since her father's tragedy, though she loved to sail in her youth.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
The shop occupies the lower floor of a two-story white wood-frame building with Tudor styling. It is one of a long row of closely bunched buildings of the same construction, which line one side of @[Boutique Lane](landmark:6f3e4291-b4ff-4380-afd6-00be23bb479d). A sign above the door depicts a winged messenger skimming the heavens with a scroll tucked underneath his arm.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The entry to the shop proper is at the end of a narrow hallway. Customers are handled by Culver at an "L"-shaped marble counter just inside the door. Behind the counter, toward the actual front of the building, are heavy oaken writing tables with slanted tops, at which Janus and two other scribes are normally hard at work. Each work area is lit by a small globe set into the ceiling beam above it (these are enchanted and embedded with Daylight spells to provide adequate illumination). Over the customer counter hangs a long hempen cord, which is attached to a bell in the alleyway beside the shop, and is used to summon the young messengers employed by the Trasks to make deliveries.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
8:00am to 7:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good, although limited in scope.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Not locked or hidden, a small bowl rests on a shelf beneath the counter, and usually contains 1d20 x 1d6gp in assorted coins and small gems.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Janus and Culver and the other two scribes are daily within the shop. There are several young boys who hang about outside, waiting to be summoned by the bell for messenger duty - they will usually investigate loud noises within the shop (usually the result of some flimflammery on the part of the occupant of the upper floor).

[h2]Customers[/h2]
The clientele is primarily guild families, with an occasional commission from a noble house. There will normally be [roll:1d100]:
- 01-70 = no customers
- 71-90 = 1 customer
- 91-97 = 2 customers
- 98-00 = 3 customers

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
The Trasks produce well-calligraphed invitations, personal messages, and public notices, and will provide for distribution of these materials inside the city or within a 25 mile radius (they did the invitations for both the betrothal ball and the wedding ceremony for the Duke's niece just recently). The cost is 1gp per sheet (additional for special inks and parchments). Almost all work is produced in the Common tongue, as the staff has very limited facility with other languages.

articles.title: Shoes & Saddles
articles.content:
[h2]Blacksmith and Saddler[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Folonar Fairweather](person:2a43fc0e-a5c9-4683-9db5-78a2008d2f72) and @[Gibbon Garrazano](person:e679efee-52f7-43af-add0-4a9fd2c6df8a).

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
This 60' square wooden structure has two immense sliding doors which are opened during business hours. A sign depicting a rearing white horse hangs from a brass post in front of the building. There is a second story half the size of the ground level. There are circular windows on all sides and a large skylight.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
[b]Lower story:[/b] The forge is in operation throughout the day. It is located in a rectangular depression dug into the earthen floor. Thick, evenly spaced, pillars support the roof and second story.  

[b]Upper story:[/b] is indicated by a large brass arrow pointing up the stairwell. A variety of flowering plants adorn window sills and walls of this single room. The flooring is made of richly patterned ceramic tiles, and there is a large bust of a warrior on a shield in one corner of the room. Either Folonar or his apprentice will respond to the ringing of the bell on the customer service counter.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
8:00am to 6:00pm (though work is often performed after these hours).

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Expensive.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Daily receipts and [roll:1d4] x 1d100gp are kept in a drawer beneath the counter upstairs. Folonar takes the receipts home each night.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
@[Gibbon Garrazano](person:e679efee-52f7-43af-add0-4a9fd2c6df8a), the blacksmith, is a tough and darkly bearded dwarf who swings his nine pound hammer like a child's toy. He often works effortlessly for 10 to 12 hours a day, without rest breaks. Gibbon is a gentle type and enjoys wandering through the fields outside the Shield Gate during non-working days. He relies on Folonar for guidance and will almost always (95%) accede to the latter's wishes in business or personal matters.  

@[Folonar Fairweather](person:2a43fc0e-a5c9-4683-9db5-78a2008d2f72), a leatherworker, is half-elven, and a smooth talker. He always tries to convince his customer's to purchase more equipment, or a more elaborate version of whatever they want. He is successful 40% of the time. (When dealing with a player character Folonar's sales pitch is sweetened by his claim concerning magically enchanted harnesses and reins which increase horse speed and rider's control over his steed.) If any customer comes back and complains about the non-enchanted pieces (at such competitively low prices, enchantment is not profitable), Folonar will deny that he made any claims of that sort.  

@[Qaften](person:98401dac-aa8d-4b40-800c-0104c12473e6), an apprentice leatherworker of great skill, is a horrible salesman. He is easily bullied by customers and often forgets the prices of the goods (his are usually 10% to 60% lower than normal). Folonar tries to keep @[Qaften](person:98401dac-aa8d-4b40-800c-0104c12473e6) from the front desk, but there is a 10% chance that @[Qaften](person:98401dac-aa8d-4b40-800c-0104c12473e6) will be alone in the shop.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
At any one time there will be [roll:1d100]:
- 01-65 = 2 customer
- 66-88 = 1 customers
- 89-98 = no customers
- 99-00 = a party of [roll:2d6] adventurers

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Heidel Varrasch](person:e28b24da-4d76-4538-8315-6a13ac6449a3) | @[Kronen Varrasch](person:dba44549-7fd9-45ee-83dd-1a94be1da153) | @[Tenley Tainley](person:abedfa62-b993-4d72-acdf-a10e5c2fc4f7) | Off duty members of the [url:https://www.worldanvil.com/w/antheros-phre3d/a/haven-city-watch-organization#Ducal_Guard]Ducal Guard[/url]

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Custom made riding saddles with tack and harness priced at 225gp, and leather barding for a charger or heavy warhorse priced at 400gp. Orders take 4 to 6 weeks to be completed.

articles.title: Spearchucker's
articles.content:
[h2]Spearchucker's Bow[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Surfey, or "spearchucker", is a real bow-lover who makes some of the best and largest bows around, with a high moisture tolerance and long life. Her specialty is composite longbows. These beautiful bows are so finely made that an excellent archer can send a shaft 800 yards. Functional, aimed fire is considerably less, but is still 50 yards greater than the average longbow. They also cost 500 Gold Pieces, with a waiting time of 2 months. 

She stocks a good number of lesser quality bows as well, with plenty of equipment. Her stock of arrows comes from Tedius and Sprig, who she views as the best fletchers in Haven.

If asked about the shop's name (her nickname) she will explain about the bet she won several years ago (see her character description).

[h2]Hours[/h2]
9:00am to 5:00pm, after hours by appointment only

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Expensive

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
She has 10 GP on hand, hidden in an old bow case under the counter. 

[h2]Staff[/h2]
She has two apprentices working with her, Nimble and Hasty, 40-year-old wood-elf twins that she occasionally sends on on long journeys to obtain the specialty wood she requires.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
25% chance of another customer browsing her bows

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
10% chance there is a composite longbow in the shop that someone ordered but hasn't picked up yet.

articles.title: Spectacular Spectacles
articles.content:
[h2]Professional eye care and adjustment[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Nima J. Neb](person:cee81c36-3d10-4264-8ff8-3566edd5aa5b), and his quiet wife Nosi. Both are opticians-extraordinaire, but they tend to use archaic methods of eye adjustment (it is rumored that they once electrocuted a blind man to restore his sight). Both of them wear their own product.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A two story white building with a large sign by the front door that contains simply a large letter "E".

[h2]Interior[/h2]
Directly inside the entrance there is a small room with a receptionist's desk manned by Nosi. Beyond this room are several offices, examination rooms, and shops for making precision spectacles. The front room is clean, as well as the examination areas, but the shop rooms are very messy and littered with strange tools, files, machinery, and glass dust.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
11:00am to 3:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair/Outrageous. When a customer inquiries the price of the spectacles Nima tells him, "20gp." If the customer doesn't flinch, Nima continues, "for the frames. The lenses are 25gp." If the customer still doesn't flinch, Nima finishes, "each." An alternate pricing method involves an eye test chart with prices instead of letters (the prices get higher as the print gets smaller). The smallest line the customer can read is the cost of the spectacles - ranging from 5gp to 120gp.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Poor to Superb (GM's discretion, based on Nima's current hangover).

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
A wooden box, in a desk drawer with Complexity 2 lock, holds [roll:2d6] x 2d5gp in assorted coins. The key to the drawer is kept in Nosi's sash.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Just Nima and Nosi. When not in the shop, they are frequently out on the town getting sloshed.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
Few and far between, and there is seldom repeat business.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
There is one tiefling who frequently peers - @[Peering Tiefling](person:d0d4b225-8e19-42c7-bc39-7a0aa7bfe786) - in through the front window, squinting as if he has trouble seeing.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
The procedure for eye adjustment takes several steps. After the extent of the problem is ascertained, the physical correction of the eyes is attempted (if the problem is not severe, a sample pair of spectacles is sold to the patient). When the eyes require great adjustment, customized spectacles are ground (3d3 weeks). If extensive damage must be repaired, an operation will be suggested (remember the electrocuted blind man?).

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
Occasionally (10%) Nima succeeds in creating a pair of spectacles with the effect of a Far Vision spell. These increase the wearer's acuity of vision by 100% to 400% (2d4 x 50%). [br][br] @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954)

articles.content:
[h2]@[Millar Lightfingers](person:1572d5bb-72fc-4216-b5e3-6138dd0159a3), Prop.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The brewery, which sits at the edge of the cliff above the river Dorian, manufactures Starkerb beer, which is served on draft in many of the city's inns and drinking establishments. Millar is a chubby, extremely red-faced dwarf who samples his wares perhaps a bit more than would be politic. Although @[Bethli](person:5d5a4b6e-bd15-4afb-8d94-fdfe0f7d6b02)'s iron and copper smelter lies downstream from the brewery, many who have sampled Starkerb beer swear that Millar must somehow get his water directly from @[Bethli](person:5d5a4b6e-bd15-4afb-8d94-fdfe0f7d6b02)'s drain pipe.

[h2]A street of artist studios[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Near the western end of @[The North Corridor](settlement:4554e4a9-db69-47da-9921-6c5850001ce8), this area is the home for many artists who serve the whims of wealthy patrons in @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b).

- @[Romulo Velasquez](person:0abd1b09-4093-4a05-9563-7ff27309b96c)

articles.title: Suttler on the Green
articles.content:
[h2]Anything you might need[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Lotho Scuttle](person:b2f58528-c6ae-44f4-bc4f-2a27c3704a54)'s shop is very large, and offers a good selection of general supplies, such as ropes, lanterns, simple farming and excavation tools, seed, and leather and canvas goods. Some of the leather and canvas goods are made by his wife and two daughters - he modestly sells these homemade items at below normal prices, though their quality is actually above average.  

 Lotho is as honest as the day is long, and would never knowingly cheat anyone - unfortunately, he is also somewhat gullible when subjected to hard sell tactics, and about 5% of the goods he carries are substandard products foisted upon him by aggressive, unscrupulous traders. If a character purchases such an item, and it breaks or malfunctions within a short period of time after its sale, Lotho will willingly refund the character's money if he returns to the shop and complains.  

 Lotho minds his own business, and gossips only rarely (usually at holiday celebrations on @[The Green](landmark:58c2143a-18ef-4281-89c4-96547a184d4a), when he engages in one of his very infrequent drinking sprees).

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Low/High.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair/Good.

@[Drungo Boxworth](person:90c26c25-79de-4c48-be3a-5088d49c5de5)

articles.title: Sym's Storage Company
articles.content:
[h2]Warehouse space for rent[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The warehouse is used primarily for storing sacks of grain and other foodstuffs. It is a large building, of two floors, with an enclosed yard in which two wagons are often stored. The warehouse is also a stronghold of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60). There is a secret entrance from the back alley into a staircase leading to secret rooms on the warehouse's second level. These rooms are used as meeting places and hideouts by @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60). The owner, @[Lazar Symbocca](person:2c51d376-29e2-4868-ac54-050e58f8c59c), is a member of the Hand, and heavily involved in the smuggling trade. 

 Lazar is rarely at the warehouse. He is always said to be "returning shortly". @[Esgar](person:35398114-993a-419e-ae0e-4b7ce65810ce), the foreman, and his helpers, @[Rimer](person:0911c4da-703b-432f-b684-48b2cfef699c), @[Div](person:3fc2ad7a-1a47-4cb1-8f1d-fb63ec7d212b), and @[Jim Bostry](person:71520a08-8760-4e56-9782-8ee024710242), are all Hand supporters, but do not know the extent of their boss' involvement. They would, however, be quick to report any suspicious strangers, particularly if the strangers were asking too many questions.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Esgar](person:35398114-993a-419e-ae0e-4b7ce65810ce) | @[Rimer](person:0911c4da-703b-432f-b684-48b2cfef699c) | @[Div](person:3fc2ad7a-1a47-4cb1-8f1d-fb63ec7d212b) | @[Jim Bostry](person:71520a08-8760-4e56-9782-8ee024710242)

articles.title: T. Barnum Pott Memorial Museum
articles.content:
[h2]Pieces of history[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The Museum is a large stucco and half-timber cottage, with a neatly trimmed hedge and lawn. The windows and door are trapped after closing hours with a wailing alarm (Complexity 2) to protect the contents from thieves. Many of the items displayed within were brought back to Haven by the famous halfling adventurer, T. Barnum Pott (What? you've never heard of him, either?).  

 The Museum is carefully tended, and its contents dusted, by his meeker descendant, @[Benjamin Pott](person:9d84b73d-aeeb-4bdf-9fef-b0a9134272a6). Benjamin dreams of being a great mage or warrior as he tends the Museum, and eagerly listens to tales told on @[Dancing Green](landmark:f2d5ae5e-52a9-4655-ac9b-49456a5196d8) or in the pubs. He has a large collection of adventure and romance novels in his cottage off West Smilax Street, including old T. Barnum's private diary, which is full of interesting notes that any adventurer would find very useful. Unfortunately, Benjamin is nearsighted, clumsy as a puppy, and afraid of his own shadow - poor material for a hero. Even if invited to accompany a party on an adventure, he will fail to show up, and can be found huddling in bed, hoping to be forgotten.

articles.title: Tael I'she-Kel - Money Changing Service
articles.content:
Tael has had his tent set up here for many years, arriving about 10am and leaving at dusk. He is honest (relatively) in his dealings, charging a strict 5% exchange rate for out-of-town coins. He also handles letters of credit, and will authenticate them for 5% of the value but will not authenticate a false letter simply to get the fee. His stamp of approval, an impression in wax of his signet ring (an easily recognizable arcane symbol that virtually can’t be counterfeited), is honored by all the major banking houses in Haven. There is a 75% chance he will know or recognize the banking house issuing any letter of credit, and he has an 85% chance of detecting a fake if he does know the house.

Tael charges a 15% fee for cashing letters on those banking houses he does know, and a 75% fee for houses with which he is not familiar. This latter is a test - if the client agrees too fast, Tael knows the letter is most likely a fake. If the client tells him he's out of his mind and turns to leave, Tael will assume the letter is most probably authentic and will cash it for a 25% fee - he does take chances, after all, and is entitled to a return on his money.

Tael's two assistants do not actually help him in the financial end of the business. Bick Dutkus and Smubba Bilth each stand about 6'6" and weigh over 250 lbs. of solid muscle - they are "insurance". Tael was robbed once and he did not appreciate either the monetary loss or the beating he took in the process. Bick and Smubba are well armed and well trained, and under orders to butcher anyone who pulls a weapon of any sort while in the tent. The last three attempts at robbery cost seven lives, all belonging to the robbers - neither Tael nor his insurance policies believe in the kid-glove treatment.

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Tambel](person:95b9c6c4-e95a-4bcf-8f75-814c0a4618d5) is a quite comely female dwarf of middle age, with very long golden hair. The dog has the ability to teleport itself and @[Tambel](person:95b9c6c4-e95a-4bcf-8f75-814c0a4618d5) up to a mile in any direction, if it senses its master being threatened. @[Tambel](person:95b9c6c4-e95a-4bcf-8f75-814c0a4618d5) has a loyal suitor who is often in the shop named @[Benngrimm](person:c5f8ed0b-ba6d-4fa9-9d0b-7ee16566c5f3), a very misshapen, ugly dwarven warrior who possesses tremendous strength (albeit little brain). articles.title: Tandy - Leathers
articles.content:
[h2]Bulk leather and leather goods[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Tandelorn Buckwalter, call him Tandy, is a halfling who prefers to live with the human folk in @[The Commons](settlement:8ff1c19a-c29d-4050-9c7c-7200f23453be) (although his cousins in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515) look down upon him, and consider him quite odd). He is married to a very lovely human girl, Roxanne, who stands only a head (not shoulders) taller than her husband. He is honest, hardworking, and easy to trade with, a totally atypical merchant for the area.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
Frame building, wooden-sided, with many windows. Two stories tall, the second story overhangs the alleys on the corner of which it stands by some 4'. A lettered (rather than pictorial) sign over the front door reads "Tandy, Leather Goods".

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The shop is well lit by the many windows of the first floor. Rolls of various grades of leather are stood in barrels dotted about the floor. Many items of leather (belts, scabbards, purses, collapsible camp buckets, etc.) adorn the western wall, while the halfling works away on assorted projects behind a low (3' high) counter which approximately divides the shop. A flight of stairs can be seen in the rear.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
Noon to 8:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good to Excellent. Any items made personally by Tandy are of superb workmanship - he prides himself on perfection.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Located under the counter on a small shelf, it is easily visible from behind the counter. Usually contains 50 SP to 120 SP, but there is a 15% chance of a recent large sale, in which case it will contain 200 SP to 350 SP.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Tandy, and his children, two young sons and a daughter. The daughter, Springviolet (Spring), is the first-born, and is an exceptionally beautiful, very petite (4'3", and slender) young lass of 16. She handles most of the sales and bargaining, and is quick-witted and very perceptive. The boys, Corriadoc (Corey) and Periwinkle (Wink), are 15 and 12, respectively, and are industriously learning the leather trade from the bottom up.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
There will usually be  [roll:1d8+2] customers in the shop. Tandy has a city-wide reputation, and those who can locate his shop prefer to purchase their leather goods there.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
There are occasionally browsers among those in the shop, but most people who do make the trip become customers.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
None particular, but it is possible to meet nearly anybody in the city at Tandy's shop.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
The leather backpacks made by Tandy are capable of holding 150% of normal weight. Tandy also does an incredibly detailed tooling job on the leather items he designs for women (purses, sandals, etc.), and has accidentally produced a purse design which includes an ancient rune of protection (anyone attacking the carrier of the purse, or attempting to @[Snatch](person:cbe65394-7605-47f0-9ab1-bcbd8d4f8238) it, must make a saving roll against DEX at a penalty of -3 or fall upon the ground). There is a 10% chance that any purse purchased will be the protected version.

articles.title: Tarmialda 'The Loft'
articles.content:
[h2]Elven cuisine - par excellence[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Skorindir Elengul](person:2566914e-1e5d-41d0-94b7-c3d10349fb3c) - is the only elf in Haven with white hair.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A 3,000 year old tree near Calenarth (the Meadow) has a wooden staircase winding around its trunk. Visible from the ground are wooden tables, chairs, and planked flooring about 30 feet up.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The public "room" of The Loft is a labyrinth of branches and secluded eating areas, lit by elven magic (the inn seats up to 300). The center of the area is a circular bar and staircase set into the hollow area of the trunk, where food is prepared and drinks are mixed. 

Any non-elf in the tree must be very careful to avoid losing balance while making sudden movements, a saving roll against DEX must be made to prevent falling, and, if missed, a saving roll against DEX must be made to clutch on to a branch or limb. If drunk, a character's saving roll against falling are at discretionary penalties.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
2:00pm to 4:00am (the elves enjoy stargazing).

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
The cuisine at The Loft is renowned throughout Haven. The prices are high, but worth every penny.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Superb, what else did thee expecteth?

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
In the trunk of the tree is a large pouch with [roll:1d20*1d20]gp in mixed coinage.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Along with Skorindir, who supervises the kitchen area most of the time, is his son Taubardur, called Taub by his friends, who works many jobs in the business. There will be one serving person (usually a half-elf, 80% female, 20% male) per 20 customers in attendance. The kitchen is manned by 4 master cooks, and a number of journeymen and apprentices.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
An average of 60 customers can be found in the Loft in the afternoon, and at least 200 will be in attendance during the early evening hours.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Bakka Hofstra](person:b54d3eaa-536b-4110-a201-39e78fa5c9e9) | @[Kruegger Rand](person:5c9dddff-792e-4a7f-aec6-92497f8d7a97) | @[Keyan Dorin](person:aa574834-5e72-40e0-a3ce-4669f30978a8)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
None. When all is superb, how can anyone be outstanding?

Aldegott Sprig makes the shafts and arrowheads. The most balanced and perfect arrrows get Carbelium arrowheads.

the blandness of the food or drinks.

articles.title: Teleril - Architect
articles.content:
[h2]Advice and custom planning[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Teleril Conindir](person:bc2a44c4-5c6e-4d5e-ab5f-46c2d2791193) - has studied architecture for 100 years and more. He is well dressed, having vast amounts of money available to adorn himself richly. His services are renowned throughout Haven because his designs confer magical properties to the structures they depict (Teleril is very talented, but he was never trained as a mage).

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A sign displays a compass superimposed over a @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) pattern hanging over a steel bound oaken door. The two story red @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) building with shaded windows has an alleyway surrounding it. The windows prevent outsiders from seeing the inside of the structure.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The shades conceal an extravagantly furnished set of offices and studios with large desks, file cabinets, and drafting tables as the major furniture pieces.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
10:00am to 6:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly, but advice costs only 10 to 60gp (free for friends).

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
In Teleril's office desk-drawer, a stout leather bag with a Complexity 2 lock contains receipts, invoices and IOU's, in addition to [roll:1d10] x 1d100gp.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Teleril works hard in his business but has a constant work influx. His son, Celeblinde, helps him out every weekend, or when the overtime hits. 

A maid from Teleril's residence comes in once a week to clean up. 

A player trying for a job with Tel will get it only if a saving roll against CHA is made; -6 if apprentice, -2 if journeyman, +2 if master architect.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
There is a 50% chance for [roll:1d4] individual customers at all times, and a separate 30% chance for 1d2 couples looking at samples and asking advice.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
Various nobles looking for good (and hopefully free) advice are occasionally encountered in the main office.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Good drawing tools and pens, high quality paper, and expensive furniture.

articles.title: Temple of Thalos
articles.content:
[h2]God of the Night; Patron of Thieves; Lord of Mischief[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Located farther down Believers' Lane than would be expected, the temple of Thalos is a cube of polished black stone that seems to absorb all the light that impinges upon its surface. The interior of the pile of menacing stone always seems cold and cheerless, and is lit only by a silvery glow, like that cast by moonlight. Most of the interior adornment is of silver, for that metal is sacred to Thalos and donations to the temple must be in silver.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
The current High Priest in Haven is Goradran Ravenswing, so called because, even at the advanced age of 65+, his hair is as black as a raven's wing (supposedly, his heart is also). He is above average height, with a particularly erect posture, and piercing black eyes, and shows little evidence of his age.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
Alain Tainley

articles.title: The Abbey of Eollana
articles.content:
[h2]In the service of the Goddess[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The elven Abbey of Eollana, was founded to commemerate an elven prophet of the goddess @[Serindë](person:fed8a554-c5c1-48cd-932a-2457b1cc820d).  Eollana focused on @[Serindë's](person:fed8a554-c5c1-48cd-932a-2457b1cc820d) role as Mother of the Gods and interpreted that as reflecting a desire to provide assistance to all women and mothers.  Accordingly, the abbey  consists of a shrine to the Goddess, a hospice for women seeking shelter or the aid of healers and midwives, and facilities for the sisters and novices of the Abbey.

The Abbey plays an important role in the day-to-day life of the elves of @[The Cauldron](settlement:983c8fa2-3df5-46b0-91fb-3dbe004450da). Its sisters and novices maintain @[Dancing Green](landmark:f2d5ae5e-52a9-4655-ac9b-49456a5196d8), and organize many of the special celebrations held there. 

The Abbess, a graceful Elven woman of middle years named @[Galeana](person:4a0286f2-d176-4622-8686-2c1f08c33cc7), is also frequently called in as an impartial arbitrator in neighborhood disputes based on @[Serindë](person:fed8a554-c5c1-48cd-932a-2457b1cc820d)'s role as seeker of truth.  @[Galeana](person:4a0286f2-d176-4622-8686-2c1f08c33cc7) takes this responsibility very seriously.  @[Galeana](person:4a0286f2-d176-4622-8686-2c1f08c33cc7) is also an outspoken opponent of the growing materialism of the city's elves. Her relations with the members of the @[House of Flanderin](landmark:cdb9ebbb-7478-469b-908c-41187de663a4) are frosty at best. 

The Shrine, open to the public, contains a beautiful marble and gold leaf statue of the Goddess (in elven form), and is visited frequently by worshippers. 

@[Abbess Galeana](person:4a0286f2-d176-4622-8686-2c1f08c33cc7) oversees 30 sisters (including the healer @[T'Sonia](person:a90fdc03-cce7-4a19-99b1-6606885d2e97) ) and 12 novices. The retired Abbess, @[Mother Kai](person:da218408-24c8-46bf-b1a4-c455a7ef066b), spends much of her time on @[The Green](landmark:58c2143a-18ef-4281-89c4-96547a184d4a), and is a favorite among @[The Cauldron](settlement:983c8fa2-3df5-46b0-91fb-3dbe004450da)'s children for her storytelling.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Galeana](person:4a0286f2-d176-4622-8686-2c1f08c33cc7) | @[T'Sonia](person:a90fdc03-cce7-4a19-99b1-6606885d2e97) | @[Kai](person:da218408-24c8-46bf-b1a4-c455a7ef066b)

articles.title: The Academy
articles.content:
[h2]City Guard Academy[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Halfway between the Judgment Gate and the Horse Gate can be found the Academy, where training is provided for the City Guardsmen once they have joined the force. The combat training given the recruits concentrates on peacekeeping rather than soldierly combat, since their normal duty is within the city walls. However, the thousand men of the City Guard are the second closest thing Haven has to a standing army since the Ducal Guard in the Citadel on Trade Island receives more actual field training in military combat techniques.

articles.title: The Aerie
articles.content:
[h2]A dining spot of renown[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Joffa the Barakite](person:418c5698-ce79-4a43-930d-c520ee28b4bb) is a small, dark-skinned man with an oily complexion, and a personality to match. It is certainly safe to say that people do not patronize this establishment out of personal affection for the owner. Joffa is an unctuous, hard-hearted individual who has little regard for his fellow man. However, he has made it his business to know what people like, and to spend the cash necessary to provide such comforts.  

 Joffa has refused to take sides in the guilder-"gilded" controversies, being unwilling to reduce his possible profits. Thus, members of both factions regularly come into contact with each other in the Aerie, frequently leading to violent confrontations. Thus far, Joffa and his Goliath bouncers have been able to walk successfully the tightrope of keeping the peace, without alienating either faction. However, tensions are continually increasing. Joffa, being pragmatic, has begun to transfer some of his finances into safe investments outside the city.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A sign posted along Chambard way reads "The Aerie - Fine Food and Drink" (there is no picture). The building itself is of green and white marble, with a base 80' square, and a circular tower, 35' in diameter, in the southeast corner. There is one entrance to the establishment, large, arched, in the western wall. A second door leads out of the tower at the second level onto the gardened roof.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
Just inside the entryway, one of Joffa's bouncers surveys each party, and decides if it may enter. Once accepted (a cut of clothing well above average, or a very generous hand with largess, is sufficient qualification for admittance), a party may make use of the varied facilities of the lower levels - including baths, massage, and a game room, or chose to dine immediately.  

There are 8 tables in the elaborately decorated chamber at the top of the tower, each providing a breath-taking view of the city. Four enormous crystal chandeliers adorn the ceiling, the tables are carved of heavy walnut and spread with delicate lace, and the chairs are upholstered with finely needlepointed covers on comfortable cushions. Patrons may choose, alternatively, to drink and dine on the lightly roofed terrace, where several long tables are spotted among the greenery. Throughout the building, each patron's needs are eagerly catered to by a bevy of voluptuous, scantily clad wenches (and handsome young men, too - Joffa believes firmly in providing something for every taste).

[h2]Hours[/h2]
5:00pm to 3:00am

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Outrageous.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Superb (even at the prices charged, this place is the kind of sin worth committing).

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
There is a central cashbox on each floor of this establishment. All are kept under lock and key (Complexity 5 locks!). By pressing a stud on the bracelet he wears on his right wrist, Joffa can transport the contents of the 3 subsidiary boxes to a chest hidden beneath the floor of his private office.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Joffa is the owner, and the young servitors are just a part of the window dressing, but Undo Hardcastle is the heart of the kitchen. The halfling chef is reckoned one of the best (if not actually the best) chefs in Haven. Over the years, many attempts have been made to hire Undo away from Joffa, but to no avail. The little man likes the treatment he gets at the Aerie, and the free hand he has in the kitchen, and has no desire to change employers.  

The three brothers, Aukhan "Flintfinder" Thuliaga, Manneo "Keeneye" Thuliaga, and Nalla "Bearkiller" Thuliaga , are Goliaths and examples of the strong, silent type each over 7' tall, and weighing in at over 350 pounds. These gents are so mean-looking, even their friends call them "Sir". Besides maintaining a strict watch over the entrance, these bouncers are summoned to the scene whenever trouble erupts. Though they rarely speak, the giants understand the need for delicacy in performing their job. They have become particularly adept at eliminating potential combatants by means of a surprisingly rapid head slap which renders the recipient unconscious, but causes no permanent damage (other than a ringing in one's ears for several hours after). The Goliaths seem to have little interest in fleshly pleasures, save for an occasional craving for raw meat.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
The Aerie is always filled to at least 80% capacity with revelers. The clientele on any moment is likely to consist of 45% visitors to Haven, 35% local nobility, 15% local guilders, and 5% other ("Ah bin savin fo dis fo sigs jeers, an..."). 

There is a 12% chance [roll:1d100] that a disturbance will occur on any given evening (the combatants in such a brouhaha can be freshly designed by the GM, or they may be drawn from the cast of NPCs described earlier in this section).

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Kronen Varrasch](person:dba44549-7fd9-45ee-83dd-1a94be1da153) | @[Boccaccio de Kammeron](person:7987c903-5d74-4fd2-ba5a-b45ef9d76f18) | @[Romano Maggia](person:816ba47f-c0aa-4d9a-afa9-161de52da738) | @[Paul de la Riis](person:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03) | @[Heidel Varrasch](person:e28b24da-4d76-4538-8315-6a13ac6449a3) | @[Bakka Hofstra](person:b54d3eaa-536b-4110-a201-39e78fa5c9e9) | @[Zender Hochritter](person:415b78a8-e074-4350-9fd9-b54322b75c03) | @[Gunter Geronde](person:e174a916-f1e9-45b9-8291-2e42b7f39268) | @[Swayze de Kammeron](person:f2d50957-7201-4aa2-aa13-0c6b197730c3) | @[Tenley Tainley](person:abedfa62-b993-4d72-acdf-a10e5c2fc4f7)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Meals with drinks will cost from 30gp up per person. Massage services are 10gp, with additional arrangements up to the parties involved.

articles.content:
[h2]A stand-up drinking spot - for centaurs[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The tavern itself is not impressive, merely a thatched roof supported by scattered columns over a fair sized area, with a barrel rack and drawer's stand at one end. Several dozen pedestal tables about 5' high are scattered about, at which one can usually find a number of centaurs clustered. articles.title: The Auction Block
articles.content:
[h2]Daily stock auctions of some sort[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Within this huge roofed area are conducted the daily auctions of stock for which The @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870) is justly renowned. The Block itself is a podium located in a ring in the center of the building, surrounded by a set of bleachers where sit the bidders. Bids are made by voice response, for the chief auctioneer, Fast-talkin Eddie Schultz, is going blind, and can no longer see the signals flashed by the patrons. The Block is a noisy place, particularly when a good lot is being offered, as the shouted bids fly thick and fast. There are seldom fewer than 60-80 people in attendance on the days horses are offered, although there are sometimes less than 20 on the varied stock days.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Enver](person:ea8ab78e-1429-4dbc-aebb-95e40bd1476e)

articles.title: The Axe and Anvil
articles.content:
[h2]Bed, breakfast, and beer[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
This is a very simple inn and tavern with four large rooms, each with a number of dwarf-sized beds. @[Oskro](person:4ac81aa2-37a9-4197-acb2-80ddeefce8a8) the innkeeper is a grouchy old fellow who suffers from rheumatism, gout, indigestion, and bad teeth, and is seldom seen to smile. He spends much of his time bedridden, leaving operation of the inn to his wife and daughter, who wait on him hand and foot.  

 @[Oskro](person:4ac81aa2-37a9-4197-acb2-80ddeefce8a8) has never permitted the girl, Dallarie, to seek a suitor nor allowed any to court her, and would be livid indeed if he knew of the reason that @[Corvin arn Boltar](person:e2aa5266-2bf0-454b-9bef-35c443361590) and his brothers are spending so much time at the inn (it certainly isn't the hospitality!). The girl is devoted to her father despite his temper, and is extremely shy around strangers (see @[Scenarios](article:088e33cf-5a28-4c3f-bbe5-a243e610d2ff): The Bartered Brides).  

 The family lives in a private apartment in the inn.

articles.title: The Bandersnatch Inn
articles.content:
[h2]A pleasant halfling inn[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Dolby Spreeker](person:97f3e4b2-ca08-4e66-9448-7e0ed2582c4d) - A gregarious, well-loved fellow with a heart of gold, always willing to lend a sympathetic ear to a patron's problems. He keeps undesirable elements out of his establishment, however, with an iron hand, and is a deadly accurate artist with a knife if pushed to violence.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A two-story wood frame structure, with many windows. The sign above the heavy front door is a printing of a strange creature composed of parts of over a dozen animals, looking very frumious (Coined by Lewis Carroll, who said it was a blend of fuming and furious. He used it in both "Jabberwocky" and "The Hunting of the Snark"). A path leads behind the inn to a small stable.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The rooms on both floors have very low ceilings (5 1/2 - 6 feet), with irregularly spaced beams and ceiling lanterns (human-sized patrons should be prepared to bump their heads periodically unless they are verrrry careful). Two blazing hearths are set in the east and west walls of the inn's large common room, and keep that area warm and cheerily lit in all seasons. 

The second floor contains a dozen rooms of varying sizes, and can sleep 1-4 halflings - Dolby will sometimes allow additional individuals to sleep on the floor of the common room.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
7:00am - Midnight.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Kept beneath the bar during working hours, and a wall safe at night - contains (60%) 1d20gp of (40%) 3d20gp in assorted coins at any time.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
@[Patman Winder](person:b0780633-326c-44b6-b03a-55f934a3e62c), the assistant barkeeper, and @[Cecilia Sandhill](person:d6a17715-6165-4155-9915-c0f7e2d5edbe) and @[Lurella Sandhill](person:2dc4ca68-9bbb-4f67-bba0-a6f6d0a8c29f), the identical twins who serve as waitresses. The twins are quite coquettish, and delight in switching places with one another at the most compromising times. 

Many of the regular customers have their own @[Mugs](person:a10a5716-43ed-4ece-be52-cfb83e10429b) hung on the southern wall, and order personalized drinks known by bizarre names like "Squeezy's Blinding Thunder". All the help thus appear to be speaking a strange code half the time. 

[h2]Customers[/h2]
About [roll:4d10] during normal evening hours, [roll:2d8] during non-prime hours, and up to 100 on "special" nights. 

There is only a 10% chance that all the rooms upstairs are full. About 50% of the crowd is comprised of regulars, who know each other extremely well. 

Almost everyone here is exceptionally congenial to newcomers, and will help them learn the sometimes eccentric way things operate here. Non-halflings are uncommon, but welcomed. The place is always filled with stories, song, and lore - indeed, once a week, the Bandersnatch holds a special Tall Tale night, with the teller of the winning story receiving free food, drink and lodging (if desired) for the night.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Chelsea Cheddar](person:64d30f65-3200-4edd-b715-ae5696d180d9) | @[Pauli Bracegirdle](person:10f7097d-eb2f-47bb-b177-ccb245033073) | @[Lotto Hamhocker](person:f06946c4-2b67-435c-8eff-844fcfd1e252) | @[Mella Hamhocker](person:6395ad3b-a481-4bb7-b38d-c20369fcf376)

Dolby occasionally gets a shipment of effervescent fruit wines from the halfling community of Spring Glade - their taste is reminiscent of champagne, but at about half the cost.

articles.title: The Bent Page
articles.content:
[h2]All night bar[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Arlog Gutray](person:ed3ccdb3-3a96-430f-80f2-843b35a835f8), a fat, middle aged man with a thick beard and spectacles.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A stone building with a large window faces Lorien Street. The window bears a painting of a grey bearded scholar reading a book in bed.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
A large public room with a bar has several booths and tables. The place is clean swept and lit by wooden chandeliers hanging from chains. It will seat a maximum of 100 people. Beyond the drinking and gaming room, there are several private rooms (by reservation only, please), and another large room with several bunks for overnight guests.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
10:00am to 2:00am.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Each serving maid collects and holds her own tips. The main cash box is hidden under the bar, next to the bouncer. It has no lock and contains [roll:1d6] x 1d8gp in assorted coins.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Arlog works as a bar tender and supervisor until 11:00pm, when he is replaced by @[Poin Sestar](person:4dc1a0d6-c235-429e-abe8-9bf6f7790dca), a wiry student of the @[College of Physical Naturalism](landmark:c437c8f9-8314-4d26-aeb2-aa298bf4be19). 

There are up to 10 well-endowed serving maids working at night, they are well trained and prompt in service (they don't mind a little fun, either). 

The bouncer is @[Urb Brassknuckle](person:126887d7-21ec-4f34-8e54-2926081eb455), a mean and tough Uruk @[Kai](person:da218408-24c8-46bf-b1a4-c455a7ef066b) (when he hits, it's like he wears brass...no, iron...no, steel knuckles).

[h2]Customers[/h2]
Folk that come here tend to be students and commoners from @[The Cauldron](settlement:983c8fa2-3df5-46b0-91fb-3dbe004450da) looking for a night on the town for a good price.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Arlog enjoys reading and has amassed a collection of over 500 books. They are in his private library near his personal quarters, which are on the second floor of the shop.

articles.title: The Black Halls
articles.content:
[h2]A small prison for those awaiting trial[/h2]

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
This foreboding pile is placed at the northeast corner of the block of buildings comprising the @[Courts](landmark:5fe07c2b-bce5-4c96-880d-d72a70bb1352). Here are kept those prisoners awaiting trial, under the guard of the court bailiffs. Occasional jail breaks from this facility have been attempted. Those which have had no inside aid have failed miserably. There are 32 bailiffs, with 9 on duty at any given time. They are reasonably skilled with weapons, and few can escape their clutches on the way to trial (it has been rumored that some prisoners have been allowed to "escape" - they were cut down in the attempt - only to save the city the cost of the trial).

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
The bailiffs make tours of the cells on an hourly basis, usually in pairs. A successful escape or rescue would require the co-operation of at least one of the bailiffs. They may be rated for honesty on the chart (roll d20).  [br][br] In most cases, the bailiff who is being bribed will demand 20% to 80% (2d4 x 10%) of the amount before the attempt is made, usually threatening exposure if there is no front money. There is also a possibility of coercion (threatening the life of someone near and dear, threatening the life of the bailiff, etc.). This is at the GM's discretion, and will usually work in all cases except the first and the last - the sneaky bailiff probably doesn't care, and the totally honest one will report it anyway. Roll d100, add the money adjustment, and determine the base amount. When the base amount has been determined, roll a d10 and multiply the result by the base amount. This ranges from 1 to 9 (1d3 x 1d3, which averages about 4. Apply the honesty offers adjustment). If the bribe has not been settled in that many offers, the bailiff will rebuff further attempts, and there is a 35% chance he will become annoyed enough to report the incident (reports will cause increased watchfulness in regard to the specific prisoner until the execution of sentence).

articles.title: The Blue Lantern
articles.content:
[h2]Entertainment and pleasure[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Kinalla Silkskin](person:d1a70928-cb42-4047-9046-a7a020a3de64) was once considered the most beautiful and accomplished courtesan in Haven (40 years ago). She is still attractive (particularly for the geriatric set), and will occasionally entertain a customer. Black-haired (with the help of a good hairdresser), black-eyed, and still slender, she has a good business mind, and succeeded in purchasing the Blue Lantern from its former madame some 20 years ago. The quality and name of the establishment have increased under her management.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A three-story building is slightly inset from the street proper. It has a wide opening centered on the ground floor, above which hangs a large lantern which glows blue (the color is intense enough to be easily distinguished even in full daylight). There is an alley on the south side of the building, a walled garden in the rear, and a row of small shops to the immediate north.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
Immediately inside the opening is a spacious room [a] dominated by a fountain which sprays a lightly scented blue liquid into the air above the wide basin. Three elaborately carved screens block the view of the other exits from this room. [br][br] Behind the screen to the left is a lounge [b] (to handle the musicians and entertainers who perform in Theater). A hall [c] leads to the wings of Theater, and to a dressing room [d]. To the right is a large office [e], where the accounting and management personnel work. It is seldom occupied after about 6:00pm, and is almost always locked, even during normal business hours. [br][br] The opening behind the third screen leads to a room [f] with a wide marble staircase. To the left is the "Hall of Beauty" [g], where many fair flowers wait to be plucked. There are usually 4d4 girls lounging about here, in various states of (un-)dress. A wide opening leads to the entertainment area [h], where wine and song are provided (if you came through the Hall, you already have the women). Theater area is two stories, and has a large stage [j] with a runway and an orchestra pit. A long bar [k] in the rear dispenses alcoholic beverages of many kinds. Meals may be ordered from the kitchen [l]. Most of the food supplies for both the girls and the customers are stored in the pantry [m] off the kitchen. [br][br] The remainder of the house is devoted to living (and working) quarters for the regular girls. The smaller rooms on the second and third floors are used for transient entertainment of clients. The larger rooms are housing for the regulars. Kinalla has a suite [n] on the third floor, with a circular iron staircase giving access to both the garden and the bar.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
As per the girl's qualifications.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
This house is Fine, and of medium size.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
The money garnered in Theater-bar is kept in a wooden coffer stashed under the curved end of the bar. The girls are responsible for collecting their own earnings, and are expected to pay one-quarter to the house (if Kinalla discovers a girl is cheating on the amounts, she simply requests her to leave and not return. Kinalla does not believe in violence).

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Kinalla, @[Bianca](person:e63156eb-0dbc-4d4f-acf6-7a26e6af346f), and 17 other girls (11 of whom split the large rooms used for residence); 4 are elite level, 10 veteran, and 3 intermediate. 

There are also 12 part-time amateurs (1 intermediate, the rest green), 3 maidens-in-training, and various ancillary service personnel (none of whom reside in the house. 

The bouncer, @[Kethelas](person:497a3cf2-8976-4be4-9294-b76687ca9386), a bull of a man with sufficient physical power to toss an unruly customer lightly over the garden wall into the alley, has worked at the Blue Lantern as long as Kinalla, and has been her best friend and lover nearly that long.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
Many.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
There is a young newcomer, @[Bianca](person:e63156eb-0dbc-4d4f-acf6-7a26e6af346f), who has made quite a splash with the customers. She is the runaway daughter of a noble family on @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b), and is a natural courtesan. She has altered her name and dyed her hair to change her appearance.
