articles.title: The Briarthorn Inn
articles.content:
[h2]A rooming house[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
This three story house has been added to at numerous times, and is a conglomerate of @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3), stucco, and wood that badly needs painting. A sign in front proclaims, in faded paint, the name of the place. Beneath it, in newer paint, it reads: "Rooms - Cheap". 

 The Briarthorn is run by a tall, broad-shouldered man with a scarred face known as @[Calder the Whip](person:2f59723e-e565-49f6-b239-3d7fae2eb0ab). He is a former highwayman, and is an expert with the bullwhip he wears at his hip. Calder does little of the work of the inn, except lounge behind his desk and collect rents. He employs four women to cook and serve mediocre meals in the common room, clean the place and entertain the guests as required. There is a 60% chance of a vacancy, and an 85% chance of rats, bedbugs, and other vermin. The thieves @[Doc](person:55e6712a-ef9e-42d7-8c81-268ae87b61f2) and Snake-eye, have rented a room here (see @[The Stoned Maiden](plot:6a3785ed-a090-42aa-949e-da36d73d4b1e), @[Scenarios](article:088e33cf-5a28-4c3f-bbe5-a243e610d2ff), Caravan Street) where they will bring @[Sigrid](person:81384052-2e4e-4145-a661-1881a2fcd4fb), keeping her wrapped in a blanket. They are hoping to find some way to use her power to enrich themselves (like renting her out as a guard dog).

articles.title: The Cleff
articles.content:
[h2]Description[/h2]
A narrow street near @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870). It is lined with old stucco and half-timbered row homes and apartments. Balconies, porches, and covered walkways line the street, with ornate wood and iron work. Window boxes and hanging plants adorn the old homes.  

 These houses and apartments are charming and comfortable, as well as moderately priced. The people who live here are all musicians, who are based semi-permanently in Haven. Many have families and children.  

 There is a 5% chance of an apartment or house being available for rent. The whole street is owned by the @[Maggia Family](organization:7157ba84-27ce-44ee-998e-007b1b0b58fa) from the North bank.  

 Residents here include: @[Largo Profundo](person:650522c3-ae93-4b5e-b2bb-43bd5ef14271) and family, @[Rosina Maloti](person:b3f1aeab-cdb4-400b-8edb-754f8dccc23b), @[Phineous Tarkin](person:22ebacd4-69c7-4c04-ab9a-a87ddb31f2e4), @[Robin O'Leary](person:a01786e8-604c-486c-8591-8716921489fe), @[Helvia Larksong](person:3b7960d3-c329-465f-b630-d0de2591906e)

articles.title: The Clothes Closet
articles.content:
[h2]@[Jambur](person:8e95192f-5952-4630-b6a0-baf8deec903b), Prop.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Jambur](person:8e95192f-5952-4630-b6a0-baf8deec903b) and his wife, @[Gorra](person:adb00c8e-61e8-41e8-80bd-4e87f5281498), make and sell men's and women's clothing. About 80% of their stock is designed to accommodate the dwarven build, so that selections in human and other-sized clothing is rather limited. @[Jambur](person:8e95192f-5952-4630-b6a0-baf8deec903b)'s goods are of reasonable quality, and should last through an average amount of wear. 

 @[Jambur](person:8e95192f-5952-4630-b6a0-baf8deec903b) is the type of high pressure salesman who will do anything to make a sale (including the old trick of manipulating the back of a tunic so that the customer can't tell that it is six sizes too large). Plainly, non-dwarves run a much higher risk of this type of larceny, because of his small stock of garments in odd sizes. As part of his spiel, @[Jambur](person:8e95192f-5952-4630-b6a0-baf8deec903b) may claim to know a number of city notables well, and will spread fourth hand gossip, and idle hearsay to his patrons as gospel truth (there is a 75% chance that any information he gives out - except at sword point - will be highly exaggerated or downright false.

High

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Poor/Fair

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]

articles.title: The Cock and Bull
articles.content:
[h2]Beverages and sporting events[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The interior of this establishment is quite unusual. Sunk into the floor are several pits, ranging from 3' in depth to 15', from 6' in diameter to one monster of 40' (one of the deeper ones, with an additional 3' high stone wall having downward curved hooks set in its edges). Around these are arranged benches and chairs. Cages of different sizes adorn the walls, some small, others large enough to accommodate a longhorn bull. Beer and ale are available here, at Low prices, everything from StarkerB to Casalli's (see Random Encounter #63 for a selection of various brews). The house doesn't make its money from the drinks it sells.  

 The Cock and Bull is the center for "sporting" events on the South Bank. Fights are staged here nightly, everything from cock fights to bear baiting, terrier ratting contests to bare-knuckles fisticuffs, bull vs. lion to lion vs. man. @[Watt Mikekins](person:8aa2e90d-d46b-462c-ba3b-eae22d922254), the owner, will occasionally procure wild animals for special contests - his neighboring businesses and the various stall keepers in the Market square shiver in their boots whenever such a delivery is made to the saloon, and much speculation has occurred about Watt's chances of financial (and physical) survival should one of these beasts break loose. Several bookies (including @[Rankim Lowlea](person:e0798b55-7900-4601-a609-6466cce493cd), see Random Encounter #68) make this their evening headquarters - fortunes (well, small ones) have been won and lost on the encounters and contests in the pits. The house gets a rake-off from each bookie doing business during the events. Occasionally, staged duels are settled in the pits of the Cock and Bull, and these draw some of the greatest attention, and wildest betting.  

 GMs may wish to stage contests and allow betting. Some of the more popular forms of sporting events are: 

 Cock Fights: (the rules for this activity are covered in @[Rocky](person:d9772e20-3fac-4d00-94b3-38a54cbc655f)'s Tavern, in the section on The Labyrinth) 

 A sampling of better cocks at the Cock and Bull are given below. The stats are listed as Name (asterisk indicates retired), Age (in months), HTK, DEX, CON, Experience, Fights. 

     [container:my-tablebox][table][tr][th]Name[/th][th]Age (months)[/th][th]HP[/th][th]DEX[/th][th]CON[/th] [th]Experience[/th][th]# Fights[/th][/tr][tr][td]Red Zinger*[/td][td]36[/td][td]33[/td][td]26[/td][td]17[/td][td]70[/td][td]51[/td][/tr][tr][td]Silverbeak[/td][td]34[/td][td]36[/td][td]22[/td][td]16[/td][td]59[/td][td]43[/td][/tr][tr][td]@[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1)[/td][td]19[/td][td]27[/td][td]21[/td][td]18[/td][td]47[/td][td]37[/td][/tr][tr][td]Swifty[/td][td]32[/td][td]28[/td][td]19[/td][td]15[/td][td]44[/td][td]37[/td][/tr][tr][td]Slasher[/td][td]25[/td][td]32[/td][td]22[/td][td]14[/td][td]47[/td][td]34[/td][/tr][tr][td]Assegai[/td][td]26[/td][td]30[/td][td]21[/td][td]11[/td][td]42[/td][td]31[/td][/tr][tr][td]Lightning[/td][td]24[/td][td]24[/td][td]20[/td][td]13[/td][td]28[/td][td]21[/td][/tr][/table][/container]     

 Terrier Ratting Contests: Terriers are feisty little dogs whose main job is to catch other small animals (like rats). Dogs should be rated at the beginning of their careers for HTK (3d8 + 12, for contest purposes only), DEX (2d6 + 8), and CON (3d6). Fighting terriers are rated for the number of rats they can handle at one time, 12 to 30 or so. Start a new dog with 12. There are a few - very few! - dogs which can handle more, perhaps as many as 40, and one legendary terrier was said to be able to decimate 60, but much of this is fable. A contest is decided on the amount of time it takes the dog to dispatch the rats against which it is matched. Usually two or more dogs are matched (working one at a time), and the winner is the one who kills his rats in the least time. Occasionally the time limit itself is bet against. If two dogs of different ratings are matched, the contest would be decided by average time per rat killed.  

 There are no actual combat rounds used in this event. Each time a dog kills a rat, the amount of time used is marked down. Make saving rolls against DEX. Unsuccessful rolls simply cost time, while each successful roll kills one rat, the result of the roll being the number of seconds required to dispatch the little beast. If the roll is less than half the DEX rating, the dog has killed two rats rather than one. Each time the saving roll is actually missed, the remaining rats have scored bites on the dog, and 1/2 the number of rats is scored against the dog's HTK as damage. If the roll is more than 2/3 the dog's DEX, 1/4 the number of rats have scored bites on him - it is possible for the rats to overwhelm the dog and kill it, although this seldom happens. At the end of the contest, add the number of bites sustained (HTK taken) to the time elapsed.  

 A dog will heal damage at 1/4 CON per day, and 1/3 its experience (see below) is healed in addition on the first day. Whenever the dog survives a contest, It gains 1 point of experience. Each time a dog kills its opponents while taking less than half its HTK in damage, it gains 1d3 + 1 points, and its rat rating increases by 

 Experience may be used to increase HTK (1HTK for 4EP) or DEX (1 per 3EP). Terriers usually start their careers at about 12 months of age. They will usually live to the ripe old age of about 120 months, but start slowing down after about 72 months (saving roll against 2/3 DEX monthly to avoid loss of 1 point. Automatic loss of 1 point every 6 months).

 Animal vs. Animal Combats: and, Man vs. Animal Combats: These affairs would both be handled as normal combats in whatever system the GM favors. In the case of man vs. animal, attempts are usually made to save the man (it he's put on a good performance and the crowd didn't lose much money on him). Animal against animal is to the death of one or both. The neighbors of any place staging combats such as these will be justifiably worried, particularly in regard to the escape of the animal(s). They are not a common form of contest.

articles.title: The Crocked Constable
articles.content:
[h2]Sumptuous meals and excellent beverages[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The Constable is a friendly and well-appointed tavern, with a well-staffed kitchen, and an ample cellar. Rooms are available, but the main thrust of the tavern is pleasant dining; 'tis pleasant enough to draw a fair portion of its patronage from the wealthy guildsmen and even the nobles of the North Bank. Prices here are High, but are compensated by excellent cuisine and one of the most widely renowned cellars in Haven, an area well known for fine wine cellars.  

 The proprietor, @[Daniel Moloxinizasky](person:a1e5ec55-38b7-469a-b453-701d7a34bdb4), watches over his establishment with hawk's eyes. He will arrogantly inform those he does not desire as patrons that there is no table presently available (even if the entire common room is obviously empty), and that there is not likely to be one for at least four or five hours (and we close in three!). The Constable is becoming definitely an "in" inn with the upper crust.

articles.title: The Crystal Ship
articles.content:
[h2]The Sailor's Den[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The Crystal Ship is a small, smoky, dimly lit tavern at the end of a grimy alley. There is an opium den in the back room of the tavern, and three rough-looking men guard the door to persuade non-customers of the inadvisability of entering. The common room serves cheap ale and spirits, and is open around the clock. There are usually 20 to 30 seamen drinking and telling tales here. Occasionally, one even catches a whiff of the goings-on in the back room, as the fumes from the den escape. 

The proprietor is an immense, ham-fisted fellow known as "Tiny", capable of keeping order even among seamen. Although he is not a formal member of the Hand, he is connected with them through the opium trade, and is not foolish enough to risk everything in any plot against them. The tavern is a hotbed of rumors and information regarding ships and their captains, and some of the rumors possibly overheard by someone who spends time listening include the following [roll:1d100]: 
[ul][li]01-25 : The financial plight of Jason and the Argos.[/li][li]26-40 : Jason's secret treasure map. [/li][li]41-60 : The reputation of Captain de Martin. A hard master, not above conscription. Needs crew. [/li][li]61-00 : The rumors of a pirate ship, Dark Wolf, out of Seki, whose actions against Haven's shipping are being sanctioned by Seki's Captains' Council. [/li][/ul]

articles.title: The Dancing Horse
articles.content:
[h2]A second home for travellers and locals, alike[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Refer to Twisted Taverns, page 73[br] F:\Bob's Stuff\SkyDrive\Gaming\Twisted Taverns\The Seeker' s Guide to Twisted Taverns.pdf

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Ulguk, a tall, stocky half-orc woman who serves as the Dancing Horse’s head chef. Loud, blunt, and incredibly efficient, she treats the kitchen as her own kingdom, where her authority supersedes even Burton’s. 

Griffen and Kerry are the two most prominent servers. Young halflings, they're both recognizable by their wild hair and rolled-up sleeves. They are swift and playful, using their halfling nimbleness to dart between guests without spilling a drop of ale. The pair are cousins, and always up to some mischief.

Milo Undermound, halfling thief | Nithi, Dithi and Glatha, dwarven refugees | Treader, halfling ranger | Vandleth, wandering wizard | Pamwell Cottonwool, humble halfling | Telinok Ruel, half-elf writer

articles.title: The Delver's Trove
articles.content:
[h2]A small, mercantile dwarven tavern[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Blankin](person:0c663c2b-8d0b-4670-93f5-8e9667eb239a), a man of medium build with a tremendous booming voice. @[Blankin](person:0c663c2b-8d0b-4670-93f5-8e9667eb239a) keeps a sharp ear tuned to the more influential members of his clientele and invests money on the basis of this information he hears in passing (if you're wondering about how effective this technique is, notice that we said a small tavern...).

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
The above ground portion of the Trove is a triangular peaked roof of heavy planking, with stone chimneys jutting from three sides, and the entire western face of the building is open to the street. Onlookers can see that the stone steps on that side lead down to a sunken bar room with its floor about 7 feet below street level. A sign at one corner reads "Delver's Trove - Good Food, Drink, and Company" - the sign at the opposite corner bears the same message in Dwarven.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The main room is comprised of an open center section (seating for 60 and additional standing room), booths (sitting up to 6 each) along the north and south walls. The bar stands in the rear of the room, and is flanked on both sides by stairs leading down to the kitchen and a small dining room (seating for 25).

[h2]Hours[/h2]
11:00am - 11:00pm

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
A coffer is clearly visible behind the bar, empty and trapped with a poison hasp. @[Blankin](person:0c663c2b-8d0b-4670-93f5-8e9667eb239a) actually keeps his money in a large jar which sits in a recessed space in the nearby shelving.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
This is a family run business, as two of @[Blankin](person:0c663c2b-8d0b-4670-93f5-8e9667eb239a)'s three sons, @[Torin](person:fc5ff88a-6bb9-4d5a-82ae-73752a150aad) and Hankin (the third, Fessig, works for @[Valli](person:34c3d4c1-63aa-40e4-84f3-ce75cdb96fee) the armorer) wait on tables in the dining room and bar (both are efficient, very serious-minded lads, who appear to have no sense of humor whatsoever), while his wife Maybel does the cooking. 

Unbelievably, none of the four have a single distinguishing characteristic or personality quirk of interest to anyone; although, the presence of four such hopelessly normal people in such close proximity might suggest that some malevolent scoundrel is conspiring to force bland reality upon an otherwise fantastic universe.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
The establishment is fairly full at lunchtime and the dinner hour and relatively empty otherwise. Given the much rowdier atmosphere of @[The Stone Hammer](landmark:bc6496c4-1ba0-4a37-9992-4e15a3f097a8), the Trove attracts precious few adventurers.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Eldri](person:b8240f19-94be-44ec-9e68-d2bf0235f2bb) | Any of the @[Disaffected Artisans](organization:61f0b977-2ded-4c78-9624-06db0fe627f1)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
None.

articles.title: The Dreamseller's
articles.content:
[h2]Potions for a Price[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Lucius the Claw](person:5a28edf4-9faf-477d-9cca-52216c7b4d56), a tall, cadaverously thin man, with sallow skin, a totally bald head, and deep, sunken eyes. His long robes are worn, and bear faded mystical runes. Lucius' fingers are gnarled and claw-like from some disease of the joints, and he walks with effort, leaning on an oaken staff.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A ramshackle three-floor house. A rickety outside stairway leads to the second floor flat where Lucius lives and conducts his "business". There is no sign.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
Lucius does his business, mostly in opium, from the front room of his second floor flat. The front room contains a rough table and chairs, a worktable set up for budget alchemy and preparing potions, shelves containing various herbs and other ingredients, a long bench, a fireplace, and a locked chest. Two doors lead to two small rooms in the back. One serves as Lucius' bed chamber, and the other as a place to let customers sleep off the effects of certain potions.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
Extremely erratic, depending on supply and Lucius' mood; 60% chance of being open for business between 10:00 am and 4:00 pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Average

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Lucius uses the locked trunk to store some cash, when customers or others are present. However, he keeps most of his cash (1d10 x 10 GP) in a metal box hidden beneath a loose stone in the fireplace. The locked chest has an alarm, that will summon three muscular fellows from downstairs to the rescue. Lucius pays them as extra security.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Just Lucius.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
25% chance of another customer in the front. There is a 10% chance that one of Lucius' suppliers has come to make a delivery.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Lucius stocks primarily opium, and potions to induce sleep, reduce pain, etc. These and other legal concoctions are kept in a locked cabinet in the front room. The more powerful and dangerous drugs are hidden under a loose floor board in Lucius' bedroom, and include potions and powders to induce ferocity, or to break down the will, as well as certain addictive drugs and poisons.

articles.title: The Ducal Arms Theater
articles.content:
[h2]Play on Words[/h2]

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
The grandest theater in Haven, a magnificent marble edifice with graceful columns and extensive carvings of scenes from famous plays. The Ducal Arms are carved on a huge stone shield high above the doors.  [br][br] The interior is no less lavish, with marble parquet floors, rich paneling and woodwork on the staircase bannisters, and great tapestries hanging in the lobby. The seats in the upper boxes are padded, with leather upholstery, and the ceiling of Theater is covered with a magnificent allegorical painting.  [br][br] Seats in orchestra are 5-10gp. Balcony seats are 15gp, and boxes (with room for 8) are 100gp.  [br][br] The cash box has only sufficient cash to make change. Most cash is magically transported to a safe location in the offices backstage almost as soon as it is received.  [br][br] Presently the show is "The King of the Beggars", starring @[Largo Profundo](person:650522c3-ae93-4b5e-b2bb-43bd5ef14271) and Salvia Bells. A most tragic story told in a song.

articles.title: The Dwarrow Smithy
articles.content:
[h2]@[Dagar Oakenhaft](person:92f8a372-a6e0-415e-b494-22d7f13ba413), Prop.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Dagar is rather slight for a smithy but the red-bearded dwarf is no less powerful for his lack of girth (his secret is tremendous upper arm strength). He works at a forge mounted on a large, rectangular wooden platform, under a partially open wood canopy. This pavilion is located in the shade of three immense linden trees, in one of the few areas of green in @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954). Dagar is newlywed, and totally and completely infatuated with his new bride, Merian (found for him by Meydal) - he may be convinced to trade his services for a traveler's small trinket, if he thinks it will brighten Merian's eye. The pedestal for Dagar's forge, unbeknownst to him, hides a mighty religious talisman (see North Corridor, Scenarios).

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good

articles.title: The Feather and Frock
articles.content:
[h2]Clothing and adornment for milady[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
This store tends to a clientele of medium wealthy merchant and guild wives. The styles are relatively up-to-date (usually only three to four months behind), and there is a fairly reasonable selection, any of which can be tailored to a perfect fit in just a few hours. @[Katryn Khatt](person:2c09b948-5496-4d45-882c-1333d3b32a23), called Kitty by her close friends, employs six other women to aid her, and does a brisk business. There are usually 15 to 20 women in the salon, trying dresses and chapeaux. The store is open from 10:00am to 7:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Costly. Frocks may cost as little as 25gp for a simple fashion and chapeaux run from 10gp up.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair to Excellent.

articles.title: The Fluttering Veil
articles.content:
[h2]Wenches and wine[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The Fluttering Veil (known as the Tattered Veil to many of the locals) is a dirty, low class bordello, a sleazy imitation of the more elaborate establishments on @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c). The bordello is run by @[Rabon](person:5dbcbcfc-bc8c-495c-b142-2d4c7edcf274), a lecherous, sour faced man who cares little for his "girls", save for their bodies and the money they bring in. Not surprisingly, the Fluttering Veil has a high turnover, and @[Rabon](person:5dbcbcfc-bc8c-495c-b142-2d4c7edcf274) is always on the alert for new "girls". Nor does it matter much to him how he gets them. He has been known to buy indentures, or use other illegal methods, such as kidnapping, to keep his bordello well-stocked. 

 Most of the girls are human, with some chances of a tiefling or half-orcish girl (see Street of Veils for details on designing courtesans and bordellos. The Fluttering Veil is a LOW house). 

 The bordello is in two adjoining row houses that have been made into one building. There is only one door, and all other doors and windows on the first floor have been boarded up. The first floor has a kitchen, a private "viewing" room, and a dimly lit pub that serves beer and cheap wine, where the girls are on display. Stairs lead up to girl's @[Tiny](person:f75ef7a2-2d1e-48f5-970d-ddf2a76c55a4) cubby-holes on the second floor, payment in advance, please. A bouncer is usually on hand to deal with unruly customers or uncooperative employees.

articles.title: The Four of Swords
articles.content:
[h2]Hospice for mercenaries[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The sign hanging outside this large, sprawling 3- story complex of stone and half-timber is that of a knight lying on his tomb, with one sword beside him, and three more hanging over him. Run by @[Marcus Ambrosius](person:c7c24aa3-94a5-4ed9-9f01-4a1bdf903d3c), a retired mercenary, the Four of Swords is primarily a hostel for mercenaries, providing rooms, simple meals, hospital care if required, and a bath-house. Most of the residents are members of one of the several @[Mercenary Companies](organization:1f566952-526a-46ee-924e-c5f90b98505b) that have become common sights in Haven of late, although such membership is not required for admittance. 

 The hostel is a good place to hire additional muscle for dangerous expeditions, to make contact with some of the @[Mercenary Companies](organization:1f566952-526a-46ee-924e-c5f90b98505b), or to hire guards for caravans. The GM should note, however, that quality fighting men do not come cheap, and the more experienced the fighter, the more his services will cost (see @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870) for details on hiring mercenaries). The mercenaries are also a good source of information on the safety of roads, and the growing orc menace in the mountains.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Kiroc](person:494bc70b-ba36-45cf-b9cf-df77d081ea03) | @[Silverthorne](person:6314ff3e-fadd-42ba-aa6c-bf26fc2767bc)

articles.title: The Four Ox Team
articles.content:
[h2]A stockman's paradise[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Another watering hole frequented by wranglers and stockmen, this establishment is neither as popular nor as quiet as @[The Iron Horse](landmark:2f1d2dba-f8ec-414f-9325-157bf94e12a9). There is a 15% chance for a brawl to break out every half-hour, as various herdsmen warm to the rebuttal in their debates about animal quality and worth. He is usually fairly successful in these endeavors.

@[Roderick](person:887fb36c-3ce1-42c2-8717-33d69d6c74c0)

articles.title: The Fox and Goose
articles.content:
[h2]A pleasant sojourning spot[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Randy Shuttlecock](person:ec41aaf5-d837-4fbb-8d9e-fcd8a62650f6) lives up to both his names. It is said that he has sampled all the regulars in all of the houses on Silk Veils. He is middle-aged, and quite handsome. Keeping in trim is his second favorite hobby. He can usually be found at the tavern between 8:00am and 6:00pm.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
The tavern is located on the lower floor of a large two-story Tudor-styled building. The entrance is on the corner. Over the doors hangs a sign depicting a fox dragging a goose in its mouth.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The common room is large and airy, lit by many windows along the south and west sides of the building. The bar is placed along the north wall of the common room, and runs the entire length of the room. Seating space is available for some 250 customers.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
24 hours a day.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Randy keeps a small iron-bound box under the bar at the east end.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
There are 3 shifts of servitors at the tavern. Randy has selected two people he trusts to keep the place open around the clock. There are about 10 serving wenches on each shift, most of them aspiring actresses from around Gambol Street. With the availability of company on @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c), the girls seldom solicit trade.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
The common room is normally about half full, with very limited seating from 4:00pm to 2:00am.

articles.title: The Golden Ducat
articles.content:
[h2]A fine inn for rich nobility[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Leander Perkins](person:6a16ce52-206b-4144-96cf-15d86f9662bd) is a red-faced man with thinning white hair. He wears spectacles, a satin waistcoat, and a ruffled shirt (as part of his habiliment). Fawning and sycophantic to visiting lords, he is stiff-lipped and imperious when dealing with non-nobles. He makes much of the fact that he is often invited to the affairs held by nobles, and is a vocal supporter of the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c) (they, in turn, treat the Ducat with deference, and as a safe meeting place).  

 Leander has a discerning eye for quality in fabrics and jewelry. In his personal quarters, he maintains a library of historical volumes (primarily biographical works on great families). Though his official working hours are 8:00am to 8:00pm, he frequently (60% of the time) spends his evenings conversing with the guests in the main sitting room.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
The main building is a large three-story structure of stucco, painted white, with trim in slats of a dark wood, surrounded by flowering shrubs and graceful old trees. There are many windows, and a dozen pairs of doors, each leading onto a small railed balcony, spaced regularly about the second and third stories. A sign on a post in the front yard depicts a lordly gentleman alighting from a formal carriage, and identifies the names of the inn and its proprietor. A graveled roadway leads around to a stable and carriage house in the rear.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The main floor contains a sitting room, a tea room, kitchen, and a formal dining area. The huge marble central staircase leads to the 12 large suites on the upper floors. All rooms are panelled with a darkly golden wood. The large crystal chandeliers in the sitting room and dining area seem to bring forth a glow from this panelling. The entire establishment is furnished sumptuously. However, some of the carpeting and upholstered furniture is fraying slightly around the edges, mute evidence that the heyday of the Ducat is passing.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
The inn is open for arrivals 24 hours a day, but most guests arrive in the afternoon.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Outrageous. Suites are 10gp per person per night (one's servants and retainers may occupy the same room for only an additional 3gp each per night). Meals in the dining area run from 8gp per person up. The tea room is the least expensive of the lot, but high tea in the afternoon (served buffet style) is 5gp per person.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Hidden behind a secret panel in the wall of Leander's personal sitting room (not the main one), it contains (2d10 x 25)gp in assorted coins and small gems. The box is trapped, and releases a poison gas (Level 16; 2d8 damage to all within 10'), unless opened with a special S-shaped key from Leander's key ring.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
There are two main staff members besides Perkins, although there are a small horde of maids tidying and cleaning during the day. 

The night assistant, @[Harlequin Bussbender](person:a913ef52-9fca-4441-88fd-a736d7c15c1f), is a youth of 20, blond-haired and blue-eyed. He works a variety of jobs between 4:00pm and 2:00am (the official closing hour for the inn), tending the front desk, serving meals and drinks, and answering guest demands for services or repairs. He is sometimes lackadaisical in performing his duties, which earns him regular tongue-lashings from Perkins. The son of an affluent mercantile family, he dreams of someday running off with a beautiful noblewoman. He has excellent skills with thrown missile weapons, and an instinctive knack for repairing mechanical implements.  

The chef, @[Haldo Rumbutter](person:a8b80e1c-8f1f-4035-915b-50a2cc0f7b19), is an exceedingly rotund halfling who recognizes only one chef, Undo Hardcastle (the Aerie), as his peer. He is exceptionally perturbed by all the recent uproar in @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) about the cooking feats of Biggs Oldbuck, and the mere mention of the latter's name when Haldo is in earshot is a good way to guarantee a badly burned meal.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
On any given day, there is a 10% chance that the inn will be completely full; otherwise,  [roll:1d7+2] of the suites will be occupied by an assortment of visiting nobles. Nearly half of the guests will spend at least part of the evening in the sitting room and/or dining room.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
Only Harlequin, when he starts daydreaming.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Margery Savonna](person:932609a3-02d8-4138-a3a1-0fab988a932e) | @[Paul de la Riis](person:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03) | @[Antonio Berensten](person:ec8f50d3-84f6-48a6-95d0-d7d6b5b65cb8) | @[Mathilde Hochritter](person:73dc6f37-7bc6-44e5-855c-981da5ad4ed2) | @[Falstaff of Borrinstorr](person:25385ea6-3ae8-4aa4-ac69-8628f498adb0) | @[Gunter Geronde](person:e174a916-f1e9-45b9-8291-2e42b7f39268) | Any of The @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
The menus in the dining room often include freshly caught local game, hard-to-get seafood items, and other delicacies. Musical entertainment is provided nightly in the sitting room (Leander is trying to introduce appreciation of the "finer things in life" to the residents of the Heights). If requested, Leander will provide @[Blacksmith](landmark:7cfb1b0f-92fe-4da7-8d2b-1fa59f1b6aa0) services, barbering, and other special guest need (for a slight extra fee, of course).

articles.title: The Golden Goblet
articles.content:
[h2]Drinking equipment galore[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Racks of goblets, @[Mugs](person:a10a5716-43ed-4ece-be52-cfb83e10429b), steins, cups, horns, and virtually any description of drinking vessel imaginable line the walls and the stands scattered throughout the shop's sales room. The more expensive equipment is kept toward the rear, and there is a young loiterer browsing about the store who is actually a guard. "Guzzler" Gohegan, the owner, a fat little man who is never found without a mug in his hand (usually partially full of beer), is normally behind the counter in the rear (near the expensive gold, silver, and glass). He keeps a keg of beer handy, and will occasionally (when he sees the person is truly interested in buying a particular item) invite the man to fill the vessel and "try it on for size." Guzzler buys all of his stock from other sources. He does not make any himself, but has a good eye for what will sell. The shop is usually open from 12:00noon 'til 8:00pm; Guzzler has a small apartment located on the upper floor of the two-story frame building in which the shop is located.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good to Excellent. Guzzler often has access to some of @[Tacobur](person:c721435d-0ec1-4fd3-aeb0-6d498aafd814)'s (Minotaur Metalworks, The Dwarrow) rejects.

articles.title: The Green Gryphon
articles.content:
[h2]A quiet pub[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The Gryphon is in a little better shape than neighboring buildings. It has a stone first floor and stucco and half-timber on the overhanging second floor with green shuttered windows. A gryphon is painted on the door in green paint. 

 The proprietor of the Gryphon is @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1) d'Emil, a lean, sinister man garbed in black, dark haired and bearded, who has never been known to smile except after killing someone (rumor has it that killing is something that @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1) is very good at). Violence is very rare at the Gryphon, however, as @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1) has been known to have brawlers quieted - permanently. 

 @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1) does no serving of customers, leaving that task to three attractive "barmaids", who also entertain customers upstairs - after clearing it with @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1) first, of course.

articles.title: The Grey Halls
articles.content:
[h2]The Main Prison[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The Judgment Gate of Haven is so called since its portals bid a last farewell to condemned criminals as they are taken to final judgment on @[Gallows Hill](landmark:0be95441-47bc-4662-9b2e-d5d0fd95ef5d), just outside the gate. From the forbidding pile of the Grey Halls, the old fortress that now serves as Haven's prison, the tumbril rolls on Friday, the traditional day for executions, carrying feckless wights on their last ride. It is said that there has never been a successful escape from the Grey Halls themselves, although on occasion a convicted and condemned felon has been snatched from the tumbril and spirited away. Entrance through the formidable gates of the dismal hill of streaked grey stone usually sounds the final knell for malefactors - in most cases they are simply never seen again. 

Truly it is said in the city that there has never been a successful escape from the Grey Halls - one can not escape from this captivating incarceratorium. One can, however, be rescued, and many prisoners have been. The most common method is to wait until the poor wretch is taken out to @[Gallows Hill](landmark:0be95441-47bc-4662-9b2e-d5d0fd95ef5d) to be hung, and make the attempt just outside the city wall. If the poor wretch is not to be executed, the problem is much harder. Breaking someone out of the Grey Halls requires the services of a well-trained and heavily outfitted mercenary company. Or . . . someone on the inside.

The actual dungeons of the old fortress, where the poorest of the long term prisoners are incarcerated, are on the lowest two levels. A number of prisoners are lodged in the towers and upper levels (some in relative comfort, since they have fair amounts of money to spend). Such debtors as are currently held are usually kept on the ground level. 

Turnover in guards at the prison Is quite high, even though the trainees at @[The Academy](landmark:4bdf469a-ba1e-4ef0-80b4-aa67f33878af) are required to take turns at the prison as part of their training. It is known that there has been one case where a man took a job as a guard at the Grey Halls, worked his way up to a position of trust and prominence (requiring over two years), and let six prisoners out one night when he was the watch chief - needless to say, he left with them. 

The guard contingent alone hardly seems enough to prevent a mass breakout from the prison. However, these men are supplemented by several ingeniously placed and reasonably powerful enchantments. It is left to the GM's imagination for the spells themselves, but while they are very effective they tend not to be totally lethal, simply disabling. These devices are moved from time to time to prevent the city's criminal population from solving their puzzle completely.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
[ul]
[li][b]@[Turin Khaey](person:8c4f7bc1-4696-4be1-b3f4-3e24f0c68fa8):[/b] One of the best commandants the prison has had in many years. While he does not believe in coddling criminals, neither does he believe in torturing them.
[li][b]@[Recci](person:c1029b09-c212-4409-b220-043204ac40a8) the Beast:[/b] Prison watch commander; the knickname fits.
[li][b]@[Benni Couldro](person:aaf2f3ea-ce55-4985-b245-f2aa4961fbc1):[/b] Guard. A half-orc who lives in @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee); he is greedy, and would like sufficient money to get out of the area. Can usually be found on Silk Veils trying to get a little cheap action. See @[The Rescue Attempt](plot:226319b0-e928-43f5-ab74-bb3e6df90e77).
[li][b]@[Brodeen](person:05f7652f-9c2c-4d39-b084-338381ac9e20):[/b] Guard. A blandly complexioned and totally average man in all ways, likes @[The Cock and Bull](landmark:a92c80a2-8982-4475-904a-1963de9ba84f), and loses lots of money there. See @[The Rescue Attempt](plot:226319b0-e928-43f5-ab74-bb3e6df90e77).
[li][b]@[Credence Bond](person:c8dc47a1-63a4-4c74-8978-9d5d8fc3d975):[/b] Guard. A dark complexioned, dark haired man of melancholy countenance, can usually be found in the evenings at @[The Golden Sovereign](landmark:12c8afeb-dcf8-41e6-bc8b-c1e790cfc048). See @[The Rescue Attempt](plot:226319b0-e928-43f5-ab74-bb3e6df90e77).
[li][b]@[Roderick](person:887fb36c-3ce1-42c2-8717-33d69d6c74c0):[/b] Guard.  A slender black haired man with a mangled left hand, can normally be found In the evenings at any of four taverns in the area of the @[Horse Market](settlement:3987cb08-4abd-4e55-a582-128df2ff71db): @[The Arrow's Flight](landmark:e9a711e0-c34b-487d-b7e0-2fc2009a9641), @[The Iron Horse](landmark:2f1d2dba-f8ec-414f-9325-157bf94e12a9), @[The Four Ox Team](landmark:dec91351-1d69-44ff-9973-d2e8cef1d606), or the Carriage House. Used to lead horse trapping expeditions on the Golden Plateau, until his hand was trampled in a stampede. He likes to drink, and is usually stinking drunk by 10pm. See @[The Rescue Attempt](plot:226319b0-e928-43f5-ab74-bb3e6df90e77).
[/ul]

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
[container:tablebox-90]
[center] [b]Guard Patrol Schedules [/b] [/center]
[table]
[tr]
    [td:15]Lowest Level[/td]
    [td:85]
       [ul]
          [li]Once every two hours, usually starting at a half hour; the round takes 20 minutes. 
          [li]Two guards, who also patrol the dungeon level. 10% chance for the round to be skipped during the day, 60% at night. 
       [/ul]
    [/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
    [td]Dungeon Level[/td]
    [td]
       [ul]
          [li]Once every two hours, usually starting at the hour; the round takes 30 minutes. 
          [li]Same conditions as above, but this level is usually checked first. 
       [/ul]
    [/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
    [td]Ground Level[/td]
    [td]
       [ul]
          [li]Once every hour, usually starting at the quarter hour; the round takes 20 minutes if undisturbed. 
          [li]At night, there is seldom (10% chance) any trouble - if so, it requires [roll:1d20+10] minutes to resolve.
          [li]During the day, there is usually (65% chance) some disturbance which requires [roll:1d15+5] minutes to quiet. 
          [li]Six guards, responsible only for this level; only four patrol. No chance for the round to be skipped during the day, 15% at night.      
       [/ul]
    [/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
    [td]1st Floor[br]2nd Floor[br]The Towers[/td]
    [td]
       [ul]
          [li]Once every hour, usually starting at the three-quarter hour; round takes 45 minutes.
          [li]During the day, there is a 35% chance for some request from one of the privileged prisoners, which will take one of the touring guards [2d6 x 5] minutes to complete. 
          [li]Six guards, responsible for all these levels; only four patrol. Only 10% chance for the round to be skipped, whether day or night.
       [/ul]
    [/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[/container]

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
Unbeknownst to all but a few residents of Haven, there is a network of tunnels which extends under the dungeons of the Grey Halls. These catacombs are ages old, and very dangerous. Cave-ins are quite frequent, and may block large sections of the labyrinthine ways. The knows of these tunnels, and has used them on rare occasions to spirit a high ranking Guild member out of the prison. On each occasion, to prevent detection, a substitution has been made - some other poor fellow who looked a bit like the prisoner would take his place, willingly or not (so far, not). 

Thirty-five years ago, when Coris Elan the great cat-burglar was captured and condemned to hanging. He was replaced with his closest look-alike, Viscount Aristande Boleslavski, the very noble he was robbing when he was caught and who insisted on the highest penalty for the unlucky Coris. The populace thought it was some kind of macabre joke Coris was playing when he insisted, all the way to the gallows, that he was really the viscount. Coris retired from the Guild, left Haven, and has been enjoying life as Viscount Aristande for lo these many years. 

The practice of replacement is not often carried out by the Guild, just for important members who happen to get caught and imprisoned. The rank and file thieves of the Guild do not even suspect the existence of these tunnels, though all are fairly familiar with the catacombs under @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee). "

articles.title: The Grubstake
articles.content:
[h2]@[Ninar Goldrush](person:a15e3e21-667f-42d1-87d7-d6aeba64aca3) and @[Forti](person:147481f4-3578-45ab-b2a9-6c5279b4ca46) , Props.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Ninar and @[Forti](person:147481f4-3578-45ab-b2a9-6c5279b4ca46) are former wildcat prospectors who met years ago in the foothills of the Khuz and have survived as rather @[Rocky](person:d9772e20-3fac-4d00-94b3-38a54cbc655f) business partners ever since. Ninar is both incredibly gullible and incredibly lucky, the kind of fellow who spends his life savings on an abandoned, worthless mine, and then falls through a hole in its shaft and discovers an untapped mother lode beneath. After years of feast and famine, @[Forti](person:147481f4-3578-45ab-b2a9-6c5279b4ca46) convinced his partner to abandon the miner's life for the "greater security" of owning this shop, which sells all manner of prospecting supplies.  

 Ninar and @[Forti](person:147481f4-3578-45ab-b2a9-6c5279b4ca46) used to have a third partner, T'mothee who recently died in a mine collapse. He had been demonstrating a "Special Revolutionary New, One-Size Fits All, Pick and Shovel Set" with to couple of local miners (Joe and Buoy, a pair of half-orcs), both of whom were rescued after several days in good health, but there was no sign of T'im (Timothy, The Buoys).  Needless to say, @[Forti](person:147481f4-3578-45ab-b2a9-6c5279b4ca46) and Ninar are still mourning and not on speaking terms at the moment with any half-orc.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Forti](person:147481f4-3578-45ab-b2a9-6c5279b4ca46)

articles.title: The Hall of All Guilds
articles.content:
[h2]The major meeting place of business and men[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
This building serves a couple purposes. First, it provides a meeting place for guilds that don't have their own hall. It is also where the @[Council of Masters](organization:0cb651d7-901c-4be9-aa94-eaf026c22c03) meets

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
The Hall is a set of three structures, a large central building, and two smaller subsidiary wings, one to either side. It is constructed of a light gray stone, polished to a high sheen, and reflects light from sparkling high points.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The main building is completely paneled on the inside in a lustrous wood with a flame pattern. Hung from the ceiling are the insignia of all the Guilds in Haven, some 140 banners of various shapes, colors, and patterns. On each side a wide door leads into the wings, the smaller buildings in which the meeting rooms and offices of the warders of the building are located.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
The Hall is open to the public from 9:00am to 6:00pm, second day through sixth day of the week. It may be closed if an important Guilds meeting is being held.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Gilberto Maggia](person:f8abcaf4-8f94-42f6-84ea-94c3c8c1b1a4) | @[Heidel Varrasch](person:e28b24da-4d76-4538-8315-6a13ac6449a3) | @[Helvia Larksong](person:3b7960d3-c329-465f-b630-d0de2591906e) | @[Rael Gavotte](person:1217ee33-13e6-4a14-8fdb-9755b8a993dc) | @[Largo Profundo](person:650522c3-ae93-4b5e-b2bb-43bd5ef14271) | @[Hamlin Blackbourne](person:24dec529-0265-4bb9-bb8c-d6240dea4bb9) | @[Salvatore Celinni](person:240111e7-69ba-4016-8406-9251c9d52c1e)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
On a dais at the back of the long Great Hall is a large glass case in which rests the charter given to the Guilds and the city by Duke Bertrand nearly two centuries ago. It is carefully guarded by shifts of 4 uniformed guards armed with halberds.

articles.title: The Hanged Man
articles.content:
[h2]Caters to legal luminaries[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Alonzo Boarstuffer](person:b70bf51b-bf6f-4492-99fe-7cd9fe9c4608) - so called from his habit of procuring a large boar from one of the farms outside the city and roasting it whole, stuffed, whenever there is a spectacular trial in the @[Courts](landmark:5fe07c2b-bce5-4c96-880d-d72a70bb1352) - is a large, jovial man, with little hair on his head and much on his chin (his beard is waist length). He enjoys the study of the law in his spare time, and has always dreamed of sitting as judge for a trial.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A single-story building of timber and stucco has an alley on one side and a two-story @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) building on the other. The front is a pair of large windows of diamond paned glass, with a door between. Over the door hangs a sign showing a gallows with a body suspended from the rope.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The common room is about 60' wide and 40' deep, with a bar to the rear. The decor is leather and dark wood, including the bar. There are numerous tables and chairs scattered in sets around the room, and both walls are lined with booths. A pair of short swinging doors in the corner beside the bar leads to the kitchen in the rear.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
7:00am to 11:00pm.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Hidden under the bar is a soft leather bag containing (1d8 x 1d12)gp.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Alonzo is usually in the kitchen, but his wife Hezal greets the customers and helps Jinia and Kilin, the two serving maids with their duties.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
[ul]
[li]There will usually be 15 to 25 people for breakfast, prior to the opening of the @[Courts](landmark:5fe07c2b-bce5-4c96-880d-d72a70bb1352) at 9:30am. 
[li]At lunch, the common room is usually jammed (130 to 150 people) with lawyers and their clients, judges, bailiffs, etc. Seating requires a 10 to 40 minute wait (2d4 x 5 minutes). 
[li]The afternoons are quiet, but business picks up again about 4:30pm, and continues steadily (about 40 to 60 customers) 'til closing.[/ul]

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
Newcomers to the tavern are treated as outsiders, and tend to be disregarded, unless they have been introduced by one of the regulars. Disregarded means not seated nor served.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
Some of the lawyers described earlier can be occasionally found here with a client | @[Megallo Manyak](person:5560d20b-87ab-4aa0-bcde-1ccf34886844) | @[Herbert](person:00e77919-0010-4f62-be26-61226e562c77) | @[Argli arn Skibur](person:e76bf2da-7f8f-471a-8e4e-b85c245cd2b9) | @[Gordon Vickery](person:0ded2af8-fde5-414a-be70-af199a025a2f) | @[Eldorato Imbethang](person:4b0b0b39-491d-46d8-93b5-0057f7bf9a5f) | @[Kruegger Rand](person:5c9dddff-792e-4a7f-aec6-92497f8d7a97)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
Alonzo's stuffed boar is superb, if rarely served. Midway along the right wall stands a dress maker's dummy with ragged and bloodstained judge's robes draped upon it. These were the robes worn by High Judge Polder Marki on the day he proclaimed a group of lawyers (to their faces) as useless - he did not survive the statement.

articles.title: The Harp Sellers
articles.content:
[h2]Kelly and @[Erin O'Shea](person:10f6480b-8845-4d21-a6d8-e37201c0d8ec), prop.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Selling harps (by commission, usually) from lady's lap harps to the great floor harps. Most made on premises, though some are on consignment from other harp makers. Quality is quite good, and Kelly frequently uses carving and inlay for ornamentation (at extra cost). The front room of the shop is workshop and display at once, aromatic with the scent of fine woods and resin.  

 Kelly is a tall, chunky fellow whose red hair has begun to grey, but his hands are sure at their task. His newly-wedded bride, Erin, is twenty years his junior. A lovely girl, and devoted to him. She also plays harp. Kelly is secretly making a special harp for her and is frantic to hide it if she comes down to the shop from their upstairs apartment unexpected.  

 Two apprentices, Brian and Malcolm, spend mornings at the Guildhall in classes, and afternoons at the shop. They share a small room in the back.  

 About two weeks ago, Kelly restrung an old harp, made of elvish heartwood and beautifully carved with the likeness of dragons for a young journeyman, @[Vernadot](person:70250451-96d9-441a-ba4b-3d3db516baf6). He will only remember this if asked about a similar harp. He does not know where @[Vernadot](person:70250451-96d9-441a-ba4b-3d3db516baf6) lives.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
High

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
is hidden under a work bench and contains 4d10gp.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Erin O'Shea](person:10f6480b-8845-4d21-a6d8-e37201c0d8ec)

articles.title: The House of Lionel
articles.content:
[h2]Accommodations for caravans of any size[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Lionel Hardesty](person:431c8232-3b8d-48c0-aee1-8b4de10c8016) VI - a brown haired, brown eyed, chubby young man who has grown up around the family business of running a caravanserai, and still doesn't have any idea of what's going on. The family has owned the 'serai since Lionel's great-great-great- grandfather's time, and Lionel didn't expect to assume any duties until both his father and grandfather died (they were both hearty men in excellent health). He hadn't paid any attention to the details of the business itself (he was busy having a good time as a student at the University). When both his father and grandfather became ancestors in one accident, the boy was, to say the least, caught slightly unprepared. He is bearing up bravely and trying his best, but is a miserable haggler and can usually be bluffed down in prices by threats to go elsewhere.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A 10' adobe and stucco wall surrounds an expansive courtyard, thatch stables, rail pens, and a three story stone inn and tavern. The courtyard can hold up to 50 wagons, and the stables and pens accommodate as many as 300 animals. There is a guarded side lot with space to park an additional 100 wagons, and pens for another 500 animals.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The common room of the inn is spacious and well lighted (and frequently lit), and there are a total of seven fairly large rooms comprising the first floor of the inn. Sleeping space is available after midnight in six of these, and can hold up to 300 people. On the second and third floors are sufficient rooms to handle 200 people. Another 300 or so could sleep in the courtyard when the weather is decent.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
Always, regardless.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Reputedly fair. In view of Lionel's lack of ability in @[Haggling](article:16fc4c28-5213-43dc-95a4-d9dccc54358c) and firmness, Low to Cheap for lodging. The people running the pub have the good sense not to be bluffed, so prices there are still fair to high

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Fair to excellent. The pub and dining halls serve quality food and beverages. When beds are provided in the rooms, they are clean and vermin-free.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Kept by the manager of the pub and inn, not Lionel.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
Lots, of all descriptions

articles.title: The House of Mr. Rasputin
articles.content:
[h2]The Boss of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee)[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Unlike its next door neighbor, the burned out shell of Rogue's Roost, this wood, stucco and stone structure has been painstakingly rebuilt in the aftermath of the great fire to totally restore it to its former state. Its inhabitants are mysterious half-orcs, Mr. @[Rasputin](person:903bb660-6bb2-42fb-bf97-971390441e7e), and 3d4 of his muscular aides. @[Rasputin](person:903bb660-6bb2-42fb-bf97-971390441e7e) manages his lucrative smuggling and protection rackets from within these four walls, and is seldom seen outside this building. Though outwardly unassuming, the house (with its barred and electrified windows, and high stone outer walls trapped to spread the alarm at the slightest touch of a substantial weight like the weight of a human body) has thus far proved sufficient to thwart the stratagems of @[Rasputin](person:903bb660-6bb2-42fb-bf97-971390441e7e)'s sworn enemies, the operatives of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60).

articles.title: The Inn of the Seven Sisters
articles.content:
[h2]A comfortable but fairly priced hostel[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The seven daughters of Kiriocus inherited a relatively unknown inn on their father's demise - they had been raised on their uncle's farm outside the walls - and have succeeded in turning it into one of the better hostels on Caravan Street, a way well favored with good inns and taverns. The girls, including two sets of twins, are Kethi, Jania and Isobel, Heidi, Gillian and Freia, and Elanya. They are between 17 and 25 years of age, and are uniformly blonde-haired and blue-eyed, with farm-maiden figures, wholesome faces, and no objection to men at all. The girls share one suite on the third floor as living quarters, and do all the work of the inn themselves.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A pleasant seeming three-story building of stone, timber, and white-washed stucco, the inn displays a sign over the door which portrays seven dancing milkmaids. There are many windows on all three stories, with wooden shutters which are usually flung wide.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The common room is airy and pleasantly day-lit, with many padded benches beside long tables covered with different colors of gingham tablecloths. A staircase ascends to the upper floors from the back of the common room, and a curtained doorway under the stairs leads to the kitchen. There is no bar - all beverages are served from the kitchen.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
7:00am to Midnight.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Excellent. The rooms are always clean, with freshly made beds (many single beds even!), and the food is high in both quantity and quality (good farm-style cooking, and plenty of it).

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
There is a large bowl kept just inside the kitchen door, into which the girls dump all their receipts. It will usually contain 60gp to 80gp in assorted coins. The last thief who tried to steal from the bowl (one of the lieutenants, on a dare) was caught in the act by Isobel. He was totally astonished to be told to take as much as he needed, if he needed it more than the girls. Since then, the inn has been under the tacit protection of the @[Thieves' Guild](organization:08dce3b2-80f7-468b-be7b-dd5fdbfac799), and no local thief would dare take as much as an iron bit from the bowl. Besides, the girls will provide a hearty meal to anyone willing to work for it (they seldom actually make that person work, but they want to hear the offer).

[h2]Staff[/h2]
The seven sisters are the only staff. Five of the seven will always be present. They are relatively free with smiles and kisses for regular customers (sometimes, a little more than kisses, depending on the customer), and treat all who enter pleasantly.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
There are usually 20 to 30 customers in the common room at all times, increasing to 90 to 120 at the various mealtimes.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
Two or three undercover thieves are always hanging around to prevent shenanigans by uninstructed independents and out-of-towners.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
The lieutenant who placed the inn off limits, Kendry O'Mourne, has become the suitor of Isobel, and is frequently found at the inn during the day.

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
None. Everything is good.

[h2]Special Options[/h2]
This is a good place for out-of-town thieves to contact the Guild. All that is necessary is to attempt to steal some of the money from the bowl.

articles.title: The Iron Horse
articles.content:
[h2]The raciest tavern in Haven[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
One can find members of almost all the world's races as customers of the Iron Horse at one time or another. The owner, a short and stocky, greenish hued, wolf faced individual with stumpy unusable wings, named @[Gyr Windbreaker](person:b7252cba-8612-4554-8bc8-e4b1a649bd7e), is a multi-breed (dwarf-goblin- orc-avanthar) who is pleasant to all and finds animosity for none. The clientele tends to horse wranglers and stockmen, since it is so closely placed to the pens of @[The Auction Block](landmark:67b5d2df-9421-4945-8139-69de4d5ec4da), but many potential purchasers of steeds and other animals drop in here for a pleasant flagon as well. Even @[Heidel Varrasch](person:e28b24da-4d76-4538-8315-6a13ac6449a3) comes in for a tipple now and then (especially when he's organizing an expedition and is looking for wranglers).

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]

articles.title: The Ironmongery
articles.content:
[h2]Imports of iron[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Ferrus Ironfist](person:86bb103a-e092-48b9-8dee-93a075943af7), a grizzled dwarf of later years, is a retired warrior turned merchant. He specializes in importing items of dwarvish make, particularly from the inventive ironsmiths of Darnaiga, a city in the Khuz Mountains. 

 The shop is set back from the street, with an enclosed courtyard inside a stone wall with a beautifully crafted wrought iron gate, the intricate grillwork of which spells out the shop's name in Common and Dwarvish. The courtyard contains various items for which there is no room in the shop - samples of iron latticework screens, wrought iron tables and chairs, etc. Inside, the shop is crammed with items of every description: toys, kitchenware, shelves, racks and tools of all sorts. Lanterns and torch holders. And a modest amount of armor and weapons - in short, anything that can be made of metal.  

 The prices seem high at first, but some real bargains can be found if one is familiar with the quality of Darnaigan ironwork. There is a 15% chance of a +1 weapon, but almost all goods purchased here will outlast their human-cast counterparts by 25% to 100%. People from all over the city come here for the fine quality goods, particularly the pots and other kitchenware, and other tools. There is a 40% chance of 1d6 customers browsing about the courtyard or the shop. 

 Ferrus has a little office and a small apartment behind the shop which he shares with a number of cats. A iron safe in Ferrus' office with a well-crafted wheel lock (Complexity 3) contains 2d100gp in assorted coins, and letters of credit worth an additional 500gp drawn on the House of Orli, a dwarvish banking house in @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954).  

 Ferrus runs the shop by himself, although his cousin Dekkin drops by occasionally (40% chance) to help sort things out and straighten out the books. The numerous cats spend their time chasing whatever suicidal mice appear on the premises, and posing themselves artfully on the items in the shop. There is always a guard on-duty, day and night, usually a young dwarf fighter to whom the old warrior took a liking.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Viktro](person:5a923d61-c9ee-42f1-9a5e-07d95e6752d1)

articles.title: The Kitchen Cabinet
articles.content:
[h2]Fine Furnishings and Locksmith Services[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Wilham Took](person:02c758cb-671d-43db-b1c2-76c69e457633), a greying, weathered old halfling in his nineties, and his five craftsmen design and build tables, desks, and cabinets - these furnishings are primarily built of the sturdiest woods (oak, walnut, ironwood), designed with clean lines and little ornamentation. Their specialty, proudly declaimed in an advertisement in the window, is building "thief-proof" desks, chests, and cabinets. Wilham is a man who should know, for in his prime he was a master second story burglar and safecracker. He remains the overall leader of Thieves Guild activities in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515), and is the halfling to contact if the services of a thief are desired. The staff at the Cabinet can produce exceedingly intricate lock mechanisms - up to a Complexity Level of 12 (a thief's normal chances of picking a lock are divided by the lock's complexity rating in calculating his actual effectiveness) - at a cost of 10gp times the square of the complexity level being designed (thus a level 4 lock would cost 10 x 4 x 4gp, or 160gp).

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good.

articles.title: The Leaf and Jar
articles.content:
[h2]A working class tavern[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Hambo Stoutbarrel](person:a581d9e9-8381-4d64-b68f-ed54b4ead25b) - A middle-aged halfling of tremendous girth, who is always dressed in a tent-like brown tunic and a grease-stained leather apron. He dislikes working hard, and gets angry when patrons become impatient for service.  

 Hambo is extremely chauvinistic (one may note the absence of female employees in this establishment), and an accomplished spinner of tall tales.  

 He knows a smattering of lore (just enough to be dangerous) on about a thousand different subjects.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
A T-shaped structure made of earth and thatch, 50' feet long across the front. A wood-carving of a sprig of flowering dogwood in an earthenware jar hangs above the circular doorway. In seasonal weather, both the door and the windows on either side of it will be thrown open, filling the street with the sounds of loud conversation. There is a small, well-tended vegetable garden on the east side of the building, toward the rear.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The front portion of the T is a single long room with a dirt floor and a wooden cross beamed ceiling 6' above it. There is a large open hearth along the west wall. An immense pot of soup or stew is always simmering there. The bar stands at the cross of the T, made of rough wood planking. A door behind it leads to Hambo and Furry's living quarters.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
Noon - 10:00pm

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Cheap.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Poor but filling food and drink.

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
Kept beneath the bar, it holds 1d10sp in silvers, coppers, and bits for each hour of operation.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Besides Hambo, only one, @[Forindoc Bucket](person:dc35773a-f07f-4c6b-a818-8f660dd297e8), aka Furry. Furry is waiter, cook, and clean-up crew, and looks like Laurel to Hambo's Hardy (he is extraordinarily thin for a halfling - only slightly overweight). He is somewhat slow-witted, and has almost no hair on his feet or hands (resulting in his nickname). He is occasionally the butt of practical jokes, but most of the patrons like the lad because of his eagerness to please. His two loves in life are whittling and his vegetable garden, which he tends with great care.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
- [roll:2d8+2] customers during the afternoon; 
- [roll:5d10+5] during the evening, almost all lower class types. 

Non-halfling patrons are rare, and often suspected of being government officials. If one has recently been on the premises, he will be a major topic of conservation.  

The place is full of gossip and chatter. However, there is a 60% chance that any rumor heard here will be greatly exaggerated, and a 30% chance that it is utter fabrication. It is often possible to find someone in the crowd willing to undertake a bit of theft for a price. In fact, if a character enters the Leaf and Jar looking well-dressed or flashing money, he is quite likely to meet such a cutpurse under less than pleasant circumstances.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Elias Pennywhistle](person:bb48c9b2-9c19-417b-a7fa-7725f4db591b) | @[Mardo Breakwater](person:968c385d-be42-4442-bae1-f40a8cf0e01c) | @[Burley Stonecastle](person:b9238ba1-7771-4c12-b4ef-fe0d1ab75c34) | @[Benham Barleyman](person:5f9b1baf-b8f0-4273-a86e-7d1f44cd36b9)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
None.

articles.title: The Lying Lawyer
articles.content:
[h2]A tavern for barristers and their clients[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Milo Forki](person:ab82043f-95cf-4347-95c7-fbbced444c1e) - is an outcast from @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954). His father was a dwarf and his mother a goblin (is he a dwablin or a gorf?), and neither race would accept him. Luckily for him, he was accepted as a squire by a group of adventurers, and was richly rewarded for his efforts in three raids on deserted cities and monsters' strongholds. He was smart enough to invest the money in the tavern he now owns, and has prospered since. He is dwarf height with a slightly greenish skin, black eyes, and very sparse black hair and beard. Usually found tending the bar, he is known for the massive heads of foam he can create on schooners of beer.

[h2]Exterior[/h2]
At the southeast corner of the @[Barristers' Maze](settlement:ce6589a2-427d-4318-9641-17d8ea7b2641), a large stone building of three stories stands alone, cut off by streets and alleys. The main entrance is on Northgate, and over it hangs a sign depicting a recumbent figure clad in lawyer's robes. There are no windows on the ground floor (there is a kitchen door on the alley paralleling Northgate), but the second and third floors are well pierced with openings.

[h2]Interior[/h2]
The common room is large, and well-lit by arcane bulbs, disguised as torches in the sconces on the walls. There is a short bar against the north wall, with tiers of tuns and casks behind. Many long tables with benches, and some smaller circular tables with sets of chairs are scattered about. A wide set of steps on the south wall leads to the sleeping rooms and suites on the upper floors.

[h2]Hours[/h2]
Twenty-four hours a day, seven...etc.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair. Beer is plentiful and cheap ("We have Starkerb Beer on tap" reads a sign over the bar). Meals are reasonable and filling, but not spectacular (Mallana's cooking is excellent home style, but not haute cuisine). Rooms run from 5sp a night for a shared bed in a room to 10gp a night for a suite with bath, bathing maid, and maid made.

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Good. This is the favorite hostel for those involved with the @[Courts](landmark:5fe07c2b-bce5-4c96-880d-d72a70bb1352) when coming from out of the immediate area (5 to 10 miles around the city).

[h2]Cash Box[/h2]
A wooden box is kept under the bar next to the mace. Most of the girls who work as serving wenches for Milo keep a fair amount of change in their apron pockets (2d4gp in assorted coins), but tend to put the overage in the box periodically. The box will contain upwards of 140gp in assorted coins and small gems by the end of an evening.

[h2]Staff[/h2]
Milo is usually behind the bar from 10:00am to 10:00pm daily. There are three shifts of wenches, with 8 on the daytime shift (plus 8 maids for the rooms), 14 on the evening shift, and 4 on through the night. One of the girls handles the bar when Milo is absent. 

Old Mallana, an ancient half-orc lady, manages the kitchen with three helpers, and generally has a large pot of soup simmering that the girls can serve when she is off. Her cooking is available from 7:00am 'til 1:00pm and from 5:00pm 'til 10:00pm, with soup in between.

[h2]Customers[/h2]
The common room can seat 300 people easily, and usually does in the evenings. It averages about a third full for breakfast or lunch, and about a sixth full after midnight.

[h2]Loiterers[/h2]
Lots, generally toying with a half-full mug of flat beer, waiting for a particular attorney to show up.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
Most of the lawyers of the Maze are here at one time or another during a given week | @[Megallo Manyak](person:5560d20b-87ab-4aa0-bcde-1ccf34886844) | @[Huiel Farris](person:f876117f-9fb2-447d-b4b6-1a9d8a939b68) | @[Herbert](person:00e77919-0010-4f62-be26-61226e562c77) | @[Argli arn Skibur](person:e76bf2da-7f8f-471a-8e4e-b85c245cd2b9) | @[Gordon Vickery](person:0ded2af8-fde5-414a-be70-af199a025a2f) | @[Eldorato Imbethang](person:4b0b0b39-491d-46d8-93b5-0057f7bf9a5f)

[h2]Outstanding Items[/h2]
The mace Milo used in his adventures is kept under the bar. It is enchanted, and is capable of knocking unconscious anyone struck with it on an attack value 5 over minimum.

articles.title: The Mallorn
articles.content:
[h2]An elvish inn of excellent repute[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The Mallorn is a sprawling two-story structure of whitewashed stone and half-timbered stucco surrounding a courtyard. A neatly lettered sign bearing the name of the image of a tree with golden leaves hangs outside the front door. There are two large rooms just inside the main door - a pub where meals and drinks are served and the Hall of Song where one may go to listen to the bards and other entertainers. The pub closes at midnight but the Hall of Song is always open. The inn's rooms surround and overlook the courtyard, where a true mallorn grows, in addition to other trees and plants. There are usually 5d10 people, mostly elves, in the pub in the evening, with less during the afternoon. The Hall of Song can have 4d12 on a crowded night, or be quiet and empty (12% chance). There is a 45% chance of a room being available in the inn, except on holidays, when it drops to 3%. New singers are always welcome in the Hall of Song, although a non-Guild member is not paid by the management. 

 The Mallorn is particularly noted for its fine elvish wines @[Imported](person:85c3b7a4-cbd6-48b9-9b32-6f7bdc14621b) from the Wold. The inn also boasts a luxury that elves find almost a necessity in the crowded, grimy city. A bathing room, with a large communal soaking pool, hot water, and scented soaps. Those who desire privacy may tip the housekeeping staff (at least 5gp necessary) to bring a tub to their room. 

 @[Querrel Seadreamer](person:99e1f927-cb2a-498e-99ce-73dfc677fcfe), a Sindar elf, runs the inn with the help of his sisters, @[Ygraillia](person:98478629-5626-4e1b-8e46-0bda89b317e3) and @[Melaina](person:3b5cada6-ba93-459b-a849-dfcc613d8a62). @[Ygraillia](person:98478629-5626-4e1b-8e46-0bda89b317e3) oversees the work of the three elvish women who cook the food and serve the customers (they will politely ignore propositions), and @[Melaina](person:3b5cada6-ba93-459b-a849-dfcc613d8a62) oversees the housekeeping staff, a married couple. @[Ygraillia](person:98478629-5626-4e1b-8e46-0bda89b317e3)'s husband @[Torin](person:fc5ff88a-6bb9-4d5a-82ae-73752a150aad) tends the garden and the stable, with the help of their two teen-aged sons.  

 Querrel and @[Melaina](person:3b5cada6-ba93-459b-a849-dfcc613d8a62) are unmarried (although @[Melaina](person:3b5cada6-ba93-459b-a849-dfcc613d8a62) has been getting very close with @[Mistwood](person:fb5ca109-558b-4b6d-be50-4b3f039ea987), one of the guests at the inn). All help live on the premises. 

 The Mallorn is also the temporary headquarters of @[Silverthorne](person:6314ff3e-fadd-42ba-aa6c-bf26fc2767bc) and his companions. Any elf or half-elf adventurer type is sure to come to their attention and may be invited to join in their quest (see @[Scenarios](article:088e33cf-5a28-4c3f-bbe5-a243e610d2ff): The Renegade Prince).

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
Nimoyln | @[Deza](person:15748888-235d-4c37-9939-8255b0d0e4b1) | @[Mistwood](person:fb5ca109-558b-4b6d-be50-4b3f039ea987) | @[Stagtamer](person:632ea531-60bc-4699-825e-94be236d7275) | @[Dewleaf](person:023b1ad8-6541-44ae-bf38-71d4586513c9) | @[Rowen](person:3501a39d-6c98-48b2-b9e2-c5a040172bc7) | @[Songbird](person:35229f6f-466f-40c0-a0ae-c82a5ff1e977) | @[Clearwater](person:770ab959-a2dc-45cf-a329-806494455819) | @[Ygraillia](person:98478629-5626-4e1b-8e46-0bda89b317e3) | @[Melaina](person:3b5cada6-ba93-459b-a849-dfcc613d8a62) | @[Torin](person:fc5ff88a-6bb9-4d5a-82ae-73752a150aad)

articles.title: The Mask Maker's Shop
articles.content:
[h2]For Festival wear[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
@[Oriol](person:0c9b11c7-b135-42b7-8324-fa2e9fcfe681) the Mask maker, an avanthar, and his wife @[Ibis](person:31453b97-8029-4488-8028-d988668bbd4a) work primarily with soft leather, feathers, beads, and other natural materials to create their beautiful Festival masks. The masks are a vital part of Festival, a popular holiday of Mardi gras and madness occurring at midsummer. The custom of masks enables people to feel free to celebrate the night without concern over the notoriety of their actions. @[Oriol](person:0c9b11c7-b135-42b7-8324-fa2e9fcfe681) and @[Ibis](person:31453b97-8029-4488-8028-d988668bbd4a) work all year round making masks from traditional designs or to specific order. There is a great demand for masks of variety and individual personality although the major demand waits until the final weeks before the Festival to present itself.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Ibis](person:31453b97-8029-4488-8028-d988668bbd4a)

articles.title: The Master Puppeteer
articles.content:
[h2]@[Ivan Petrushka](person:0a7b733e-3e61-4347-8f2a-4aa82cd2668d), prop.[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
Ivan is a tall, burly man with a thick black beard, bushy eyebrows and a scowl permanently on his face. He speaks in surly monosyllables and grunts, and walks with a painful limp. Through his puppets, however, he is a different man. Cheerful, loving, and vivacious, but only through the puppets can he release his true gentle nature. He is not aware of this split of his personality - but the puppets talk about "the boss" constantly, bemoaning his hard heart! 

 His young "daughter", @[Nadia](person:b6ba0696-ba08-4712-bd84-c231fed16e9f), a street waif the puppets adopted (and Ivan grudgingly allowed to stay) loves him dearly, recognizing him through the puppet's voices.  

 There are around 2 or 3 apprentices in the shop that carve the puppets and work the props, etc. but apprentices rarely stay long with such a dark and moody master. Only one, Gepetto, has stayed longer than six months.  

 Ivan has a beautifully carved enchanted marionette that he uses to attract people to the chows. It is capable of independent movement, controlled magically from a distance (see Encounters, The South Corridor) 

 Puppet shows range from legendary epics to humorous; 1gp for a seat.

[h2]Price Range[/h2]
Fair

[h2]Quality[/h2]
Very Good

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Nadia](person:b6ba0696-ba08-4712-bd84-c231fed16e9f)

articles.title: The Master's Quill
articles.content:
[h2]Books, maps, and documents[/h2]

[h2]Description[/h2]
The front room of this little shop is crammed with bookshelves and racks of maps with all shelves and racks neatly labeled (in dwarvish) as to their contents. The proprietor of the shop is a bespectacled dwarf of middle years, @[Darvi arn Malakki](person:18f105db-a71f-4325-9e72-17332c993564), with bright blue eyes and a cheery voice. Darvi is more than a seller of books and maps. He is a trained scholar and historian and can read over a dozen languages, both contemporary and ancient. He is also a student of myth and legend and has an 85% chance of having some information on a given topic if it concerns dwarves or dwarvish history, with a 45% chance on non-dwarvish topics. Darvi has grown very fond of his adopted city of Haven (he is originally from Darnaiga), and has amassed a considerable library of its history consisting of private diaries, old ledgers, and letters covering a considerable span of time. He has a 75% chance of knowing useful information on the subject of Haven, past and present. 

 Darvi is married and lives with his wife Meekin in a comfortable apartment behind the shop. He has been known to do some traveling and to disappear for months at a time. It is also rumored that he has done work for the @[Circle Chamber](organization:61e67a7d-70ca-4b03-818c-e3f7beb47566) and the Mages Guild.

[h2]NPC Encounters[/h2]
@[Meekin arn Malakki](person:fe51898a-e94e-4b00-b82d-fc379c6b3371)
